slices.summary: Most of Layer 1 (capture/) is built and is in production since merge c501eec9 (18 Oct). That includes the gate that archives instead of deleting, provider refusals that raise instead of reading as an empty inbox, inferred timestamps, bundles stored for L2 (E1/E8), and Harsh's 19 Oct rebuild (1925a5bb, a8dbefa2, 0d5939d1). That rebuild also fenced the junk gate (E9) and dropped the "drop matchmaking / plan notices" lines (B2). Nine items listed in the docs are confirmed closed in code. What remains is mostly about how good the junk filter is and how much L1 actually carries forward. First, a confident `llm_junk` verdict does not stand: the parked drain re-admits it on every heartbeat, and the re-read skips the gate, so newsletter snippets get extracted anyway. Second, the gate judges "is a human writing?" without ever seeing the sender. Third, no L1 model site has ever been run on a real model; B2 shipped on answers written by the ideal reader. Fourth, a failed per-message Gmail fetch silently falls back to the list snippet. Downstream in the new architecture, the L1→L2 bundle carries only published signals, and the closed 16-type vocabulary has no word for intros, meetings, fundraising or applications. Those workstreams never trigger L2's R-9 pass, whose only bundle reader is off by default anyway. The EvidenceNeed fetchers (E2) are also not armed, so every L2 request for more evidence stays open. That helps explain "sometimes no reasoning" and thin correlation. E3–E7 and E10 are unbuilt; E5 and E7 wait on Rohit's decisions, and E4/E6 wait on the live key. Production has not been measured since the deploy (F6), so whether the 4 Oct funnel loss (27 of ~470 mails, 0 of 22 meetings) is actually fixed, and whether the resync, attachment requeue and company brief happened, needs the read-only SQL given in each item. The L1 folder docs stop at 18 Oct and contradict the code.

L2 has the right parts, but production does not run them as the main path. The parts that exist and work: a bounded judgment pass (R-9, reason/l2) with a six-block dossier, the claim check, a code-chosen lane and replay; the STEP-12 expert pass (R-7); and the L3 admission of L2's proposals. Thinking-off on all R-sites, the money tool, L1 conflicts reaching the judgment and the oversized-prompt fix are all on the production head. Even so, a card exists only when L3 has already filed a situation on the file and that situation's domain maps to an activated corpus. Situations in `general`, the fallback domain whenever no keyword hint fires, are decided in shadow only, so no card. A judgment that is refused, truncated, failed, over budget or held at admission is handed back to the formula lanes (the 23 reasoners and the per-pack rules). Those lanes also spend the shared 7-a-day signal cap before the expert's files are decided. Together these explain "fewer and weird" cards and "L2 and L3 failing each other". Held moves never get a repair call: the founder gets a fixed engineer's sentence from verify.py:787-793 plus claim_check.HELD_BECAUSE in place of the advice. The STEP-13b check fixes that cut Haiku's held share from 79% to 18.5% sit on an unmerged branch, and the production model (Sonnet 5) has never had a completed live golden pass. Under `l2_cards`, the six-dimension confidence, options, decision need and history are dropped where the result is written as an expert review, so the card still shows the formula's {C, U, I}. Admission stays in shadow and never creates a situation. A subject with no file can never become a card. Domain expertise (Plane D) reaches the model only through one Founder Office playbook, and only for files the brief names. Goals reach the judgment only as background lines with no ids. Nothing in the prompt asks about them and nothing in the output can carry one, so no card can name a goal. Almost every skip shows only in a server log line. The production state (which switches are on, held share, card sources) was not read; the SQL is in each item's blocked_on.

L3 (context/) is the most fully built layer, and today it, not L2, decides what exists. In process_pending, every event is correlated by thread first, then by (anchor node, keyword-derived domain, 45-day generation). Nine writers then form situation rows before any reasoning runs. Only after that does reason.runner.run_all (R-7 expert, then R-9 L2 judgment, then the compiled lane, then pack rules) reason over those rows, and the cards are built from them. The new admission door (context/l2_admission, fb429b78) runs in shadow only and only when l2_reasoning is on. Nothing reads its output, and it can only see situations anchored on the file's own node. Every reading situation (awaiting reply, commitment overdue, support, period, meeting, document) is anchored on a synthetic node, so admission cannot see it, and GeniOS-009 G0.3's planned first switch (outreach seeds) cannot work as designed. Correlation fails silently in several places that leave L2 with nothing to reason on: (1) noise, archived and held events are never filed; (2) a reply can inherit a reading's synthetic correlation and land in no file; (3) a bundle that is not yet filed is judged as a contextless 'seed' whose HOLD has no applier and raises no EvidenceNeed; (4) a bundle spanning two files is judged under the first only; (5) correlations whose anchor node vanished (rebuild_graph, merges) are silently dropped from files. One counterparty usually holds several live situations: one per keyword domain (with an 'admin' fallback) and one per 45-day generation. So the L2 judgment HOLDs instead of admitting, and under l2_cards the file falls back to the old lane. This is a likely code-level source of the 'sometimes no correlation, sometimes no reasoning' and duplicate or odd cards. Rebuild paths are risky: any history backfill that mints a deal node deletes every situation and re-mints random ids, which orphans admissions, resolution claims and human closes (the docstring wrongly says the ids are content hashes). Harsh's 20–21 Oct L3 fixes are real and in the code. However, the as-of read and situation_interpretations are built with no caller or reader, and the plan's 'wired' claims for hold→EvidenceNeed and for identity candidates are false. L3 has no goal object or goal link at all. Production was not read; the size of each failure needs the read-only SQL given in blocked_on.

I read the code at 0cc8d83c and the dashboard at origin/main 2edfb86. I did not read production.

What works: the card plumbing is sound. GET /cards reads through three doors: decision, team/verify situation, and question. GET /cards/{id} returns the full row plus context, actionability, the decision projection and annotated actions. The action route takes Done, Later, Wrong (with the founder's words and a scope) and Answer. Your words are kept, and the next expert/L2 review reads them. Every Wrong reason a card offers is now storable (migration 0210). Six of the eight live bugs from 4 Oct are fixed in the code (1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7). Bug 6 is closed only according to an earlier note, and bug 8 is half verified. The web Cards page with Answer and Feedback is merged into dashboard main; the 06-CARDS README still says it is not merged.

What does not work against Rohit's card contract:
- No brain change C1 to C8 is built. There is no card writer (no deliver/card_copy.py, no cards.copy column), so the subject is the expert's move cut at 60 characters, or a formula template, or the l5_render model line. On review-level cards a "Needs a decision —" prefix leaves only 41 characters for the body.
- The queue row carries 13 fields, not the face's two lines.
- The expert's "if you act now" (scenarios.act) never reaches the card. An expert card has no steps (How), and formula cards get stock steps.
- Context is person-level (the subject's last 4 meetings and 3 promises), and several stock sentences repeat, so cards read the same.
- Quotes carry no sender or date.
- There is no goal anywhere.
- There is no person-delegate route. Card-scoped agent delegation already exists (POST /v1/delegations with card_id, and /v1/insights/{id}/handoff), but the client must supply a typed play and its params, and the dashboard keeps Delegate locked.
- There is no "this is right" verdict.

The Mac app still offers Done on question cards and sends Wrong with no reason. The server refuses both with a 422, the app swallows the error, and the card comes back, so those presses never reach learning.

L4 still auto-plans executions from every authoritative signal on each heartbeat. The DecisionObject that L3 writes goes into situation_interpretations, which nothing reads. No human decides first.

Delivery is pull-only. Slack is the only push adapter, the dashboard has no screen to set it up, and provisioning registers only in_app. So the STEP-15 kept brief and the L4 reminders reach no one, and the dashboard reads an older brief route instead.

L6 runs, but its outputs stay internal. learning_metrics, human_events and card_feedback_revisions have no reader. Learning transitions, evaluations and rejections are read only by count receipts. Calibration runs in shadow and its would-mute results are seen by nobody. The inbox's moment feedback is loaded and dropped. Human-review learning objects have no screen. macv_ledger and AER are still empty.

Plan problem: GeniOS-009 G6 would serve the goal board on GET /v1/insights?group=goal. The Cards page reads /cards, and the only dashboard reader of /v1/insights (decision-inbox) is not mounted.

Nothing of the GeniOS-009 goal loop exists in code yet, and even a finished plan would not make "Antler Singapore admission" a goal. Of the ground work, only G0.1 is done: Harsh's three CI fixes are in the production head, and CI is green at 0cc8d83c. The rest of G0 is open. `l2_cards` is still off by default. The F15 wave subject is missing, and the held-card text is still written in engineer's words. L3 admission still runs in shadow and writes no seeds. D1–D8 were never answered. G1–G9 are entirely missing: there is no goal contract, table, store, `/v1/goals` route, dossier block G, `goal_impacts` field, link table, progress tool, goal column on cards, check-in state, decision request or progress event. Migration 0250, which the plan reserves for goals, is already taken by GeniOS-010 B8. Today a goal is only a free-text line in the company brief. The only automatic proposer is the weekly brief drafter. It runs only for tenants that already have an accepted line, reads memory patterns rather than situations, files or reasoning, and is told to propose only what is missing. The per-file readers that do see a workstream (R-7 expert, R-9 L2) have no field for proposing a goal. The plan keeps that gap: G1 names the drafter as the only proposer ("or later L2's" has no unit), and G2 never prints proposed goals. G3 refuses any goal that block G did not print, so L2 can only link Antler to an umbrella goal like "Get into accelerator programs". The "Proposed goal" card in 06-CARDS-TARGET has no unit either. On the surfaces, the home page always shows no goals: the live goal list is hard-coded to [], "Goals formed" to 0, and "No goals set yet" always appears, while the Goals page does list the accepted brief goals. The Goals page makes the founder type four free-text answers that end up inside the goal's text, and it never shows the drafter's evidence. One adjacent defect matters for the design: the L2 path asks the model for `proposed_kind` but never writes it, so kind proposals stop as soon as `l2_cards` is switched on. A goal proposer built the same way must be wired into the L2 sweep explicitly. Production was not read: whether Rohit's brief has goal lines, whether the weekly review ran, which switches are on and whether an Antler file exists all need the SQL given in blocked_on.

The web dashboard at origin/main 2edfb86 now contains the GeniOS-010 navigation, home, Goals, Screen and Cards work. That includes Harsh's wiring to B5/B6/B8/B9. On the web Cards page, question cards take an Answer, Done is hidden where the brain refuses it, Feedback carries a reason, your words and a scope, Later takes a picked day, and refusals stay on screen. The routes and response shapes match the brain at 0cc8d83c. Brain items B3, B4, B5, B6, B8 (S1–S6 and S8) and B9 are built and in the production branch. B1 (GET /v1/goals) and B2 (the AER/HIR rollup) are not built, and none of the card-writer items C1–C9 exist. So no surface shows a goal: Cards hard-codes "Not linked to a goal yet", the Mac app sets goal: null, and Goals and Screen list every card as unlinked. The home ignores the brief's accepted goals and always says "No goals set yet". Delegate is drawn but locked on web and Mac, because POST /cards/{id}/delegate does not exist. Two things on the home tell a signed-in customer something false: the bell shows four static notices ("HubSpot sync failed", "Pricing policy blocked 2 actions"), and "No action bypassed a hard rule" / "Policy-safe 100%" is a constant, not a measurement. The Mac app exists in three versions. Rohit runs 0.3.4 from the unmerged branch rohit/desktop-ux. main holds 0.2.4, where "Not useful" sends no reason and Done on a question card is refused, and both refusals are swallowed. The dashboard's download serves a zip from 14 Sep ("Desktop 0.2.0"). The Goals and Screen pages map cards with their own mapper. It shows the brain's verdict code ("reply", "review_source") as "What to do" and inference labels as proof, so one card reads differently on Cards, Goals and Screen. Cards look thin or repeated because the card writer (C1), the expert's result on the card (C2) and per-card context (C6) are unbuilt, and the surfaces' guard hides every line one card shares with another. Two production facts could not be checked without Rohit's permission: whether migration 0250 is applied, and whether the live dashboard was deployed before the brain dropped snapshot.notice (B9).

CI itself is now sound. It has three jobs on Python 3.11 (the same version production runs), a Postgres 17 database suite, a scan that fails on unexplained skips, and a golden set that refuses to run without a database. It went green on the production branch at 0cc8d83c on 22 Oct. But nothing stops red code from reaching production. Branch protection is off on harsh/mvp, speedrun008 and main. The production branch was red on all 61 CI runs from 6 Sep to 21 Oct. The 823-commit merge c501eec9 never had a CI run of its own, and the first run that contained it (21 Oct) was red on bugs already in the production code: subjects re-decided on an unchanged sweep, cassettes recorded on an IST database, and a 24.5 s re-read query. No test calls a real model in CI. All 67 golden cassettes are written by the ideal reader, and the L2-vs-today comparison answers R-9 by copying the case's expert answer. So "63/63 parity" proves plumbing only. The production models of R-7 and R-9 (claude-sonnet-5) and the junk-gate prompt rewritten on 19 Oct have never had a valid real-model pass. The only pass that met its target (the STEP-13b Haiku ladder, held share 79% to 18.5%) sits on local, unpushed branches. Nothing measures production card volume or quality daily: pipeline_health, runtime_receipts and l2_shadow_report are manual scripts, the funnel counters are written every pass but read by nothing, and the dashboard shows only a weekly cards_7d tile. The card path is set by four activation tables plus several env flags. They are flipped by staff routes, by scripts/activate_tenant.py and by make_tenant_live itself, and their production state shows on no surface. Migrations apply at boot, except on a read-only database, where the boot is degraded and only an unmonitored /health says so. Whether 0243–0250 are applied, which commit is live, and which switches are on can only be answered from production. The exact read-only SQL is given in blocked_on. The two branches have drifted: harsh/mvp is 42 commits ahead of speedrun008, and Harsh's 27 rebuild commits of 19–21 Oct went straight to production and changed no plan or log document.

I read all 97 memory notes and the docs named in the brief, then checked the claims that matter against the code, git and the dashboard's origin/main. Memory notes are cited as memory/<file>.md (folder: /Users/rohitswerashi/.claude/projects/-Users-rohitswerashi-Downloads-Artifacts-Product-genios-brain--yc-/memory/).

The costly mistakes are recent and about plan and process. From 5 to 17 Oct, YC-II W27 kept patching the old flow while Design Atlas v2 was the target. That old-flow engine then reached production in one merge on 18 Oct: 823 commits (c501eec9), with no production number taken per step. Production has not been measured since, so it is unknown which card path Rohit's org runs.

Every proof was taken with the ideal reader. The one real-model pass held 79% of reviews, and no step re-runs the real model before a switch or a push.

Code reached harsh/mvp while CI was red. Harsh's L1 rebuild accepted 199 golden failures as 'pre-existing'. A fingerprint regression (ae5b5c7a) re-decided unchanged subjects in production until 22 Oct.

The L2/L3 rebuild shipped before its own audit. That audit then fixed two silent failures that match Rohit's symptoms exactly: a failed L3 pass read as 'nothing to do', and one oversized prompt stopping the L2 pass. The rebuild was also never logged in the GeniOS-008 layer folders; L3 has no folder at all.

Goals were planned last. The architecture defines no goal object. GeniOS-009's only inferred-goal source is the brief drafter, which reads patterns and not the graph, so the Antler admission could not become a goal. The golden tenant's pre-curated brief hides this gap.

The founder's investor and programme playbooks wait behind a 267-line review that has never been filled in (all 267 lines have an empty decision), so fundraising situations end 'unreviewed' on the compiled lane.

The older YCW27-era mistakes (false findings, guards that could not fail, harmful fixes caught in time, fan-out quota burns, a $10.4 Sonnet pass wasted to thinking tokens) are mostly fixed; only their lessons remain. Rohit is the owner where the blocker is a decision or permission; where a fix needs a production read, the read-only SQL is in blocked_on.

Many of the decisions carried over from GeniOS-008, GeniOS-009 and YC-II W27 were answered, or their defaults are now in code: 52 YC-II decisions, 7 GeniOS-008 questions and 1 GeniOS-009 decision. 12 findings marked fixed are confirmed in the production head. Those 72 are not listed below. The open items matter because their defaults were often never built, or were built differently from what the docs say.

1. **Per-type cutover not built.** The cutover was meant to go one situation type at a time (A2/A3). `l2_cards` instead switches every file of a tenant at once. Nothing reads L2's admissions yet.
2. **Founder playbooks still unreviewed (D1).** The default was to run them labelled. Only the expert path does that. The compiled lane refuses every Founder Office situation as 'unreviewed': all 6 capabilities are draft and all 267 review lines are blank. So investor, programme, intro, compliance and hiring work can only become a card through the expert or L2 switches. Those are off by default, and the golden runner forces them on, together with the LLM decider.
3. **Quiet files are never looked at again (D57).** A file with no reply pattern yet never gets a second review, so investor outreach that has gone silent never comes back as a card (golden F15 fails on this).
4. **Defaults that were never built.** Email delivery (B3) has no channel. Human approval before planning (B1) is not wired. The STEP-15 morning brief is composed at 08:00 but neither the dashboard nor the Mac app reads its endpoint (D9). The 365-day history window (C3) is still 60 days in code.
5. **Built but never merged.** STEP-13b (D64, the engine's expertise and the company's own record in the expert's dossier) is 43 commits on local-only branches. It is not in production and not on any remote.
6. **Live defects found in code.**
   - Undated and conditional promises never reach the graph (F165). The conditional part is new since the 21 Oct L3 audit.
   - The Admin vendor-renewal situation can never fire (B10 → F56).
   - A move resting only on the founder's confirmed answer gets no card (F302).
   - Cards say "they normally reply in about N days" without checking where that number came from (B15).
7. **Goal decisions (GeniOS-009 D1/D2/D7/D8).** All are on their defaults with nothing built, so no goal reaches a card and Antler cannot be proposed as a goal.

Production was not read. Whether Founder Office, expert_review, l2_* and the LLM decider are on for Rohit's org, and whether the operator runs (repair, declare, resync, promote) happened, needs the read-only SQL given in blocked_on.

refuted.note: F19 does not conflict with one card per file, and it passes. Its three expectations each read about [Naveen]/[Ritika]/[Ekta] with min 1 and max 1. They are matched by words: tests/replays/marking.py:146-151 cards_about counts any card whose text names the person, and _card_check (:160-170) checks the count per expectation. One card that names all three people satisfies all three expectations. GeniOS-009 01-AS-IS-CARDS.md:87 (measured 22 Oct) shows F19 as pass with 1 card ('decision · Answer the cell's three asks today (v2)') on both paths. The contract already accepts D58's recommended shape.

critic_summary: I checked the existing list against the code. Four gaps are verified and new; each comes with evidence, and three include production SQL. The biggest one is billing. Since commit 7075014c (4 Oct, already in production before the 18 Oct merge), the scheduled sweep skips the whole L1 to L5 chain for any org whose trial has lapsed, and the warm lane refuses that org's events too. That same commit's message measured "Rohit Swerashi, grace closed 21 Sep". Nothing in the repo or the docs shows his plan was extended afterwards. The dashboard's "Sync now" job checks neither plan expiry nor the ingestion quota, so on a lapsed org cards would appear only when someone presses Sync. That would explain both "fewer" and "sometimes". The ingestion quota and the daily model cap can also stop the sweep without anyone seeing it, and the 365-day resync can fill the quota. Second, the question-card fix from STEP-13 was applied to only one reader, the Cards queue. Home "Today", the MCP connector, the agent API, both push lanes, /v1/insights (where G6 plans the goal board), Ask and the Context panel all read decision cards only. Third, post-meeting follow-up cards (capability "meeting.followup") fail all three doors. They never reach GET /cards, and opening one gives a 404. Fourth, "Sync now" runs a second copy of the chain. It writes no funnel numbers and runs no meeting, team or verify post-pass, so a production funnel read would undercount exactly the passes Rohit triggers by hand. Whether these happen in production depends on the plan columns, sync jobs and transcripts. I did not read production; the SQL is in blocked_on.

items.title: A mail the junk filter archived as llm_junk is re-admitted on every heartbeat and extracted from its list snippet, skipping the gate
items.expected: A junk disposition is a recorded verdict that stands until a gate re-judges it, and an archived mail is 'read by no model'. Re-judging should mean running the current gate again on the full body.
items.expected_source: speedrun008/YC-II W27/08-FOR-HARSH-deploy-and-after.md:582 (archive = read by no model); 05-BLUEPRINT Part 7 'Filter accountability'; YC-II W27/03-FINDINGS.md:76 F55 (whether the filter's verdict should stand left to STEP-07)
items.actual: drain_parked runs on every heartbeat (routes.py:1450; limit 200; no org filter) and treats llm_junk and llm_junk_unconfident as RE_ADJUDICABLE (drain.py:44-49). Every archived llm_junk mail that has a payload (archives keep one: pipeline.py:1679-1701) is flipped to outcome='emitted', route='needs_extraction' without running the gate (drain.py:166-247). queue_unread then files it into the re-read ladder (unread.py:338-389), and a re-read skips S2 (gate.py:166-179). On the Gmail fast path a confident drop is never full-fetched, so its stored payload holds only the list fields and snippet (composio.py:602-628). Result: the junk filter delays mail rather than filtering it, and marketing snippets become extraction claims (L3 below_floor lane) and can publish signals.
items.fix: Re-admission must re-judge, not skip the judge. The drain re-admits an llm_junk archive only when the gate's prompt version has changed since the verdict, and then it full-fetches the body and runs the current gate (the S2 skip for re-reads must not apply to these). Otherwise the archive stays archived. Add a test on the drain→re-read path and a mutation that brings back the bypass. Correct the 08 runbook line.
items.effect_on_cards: Weird cards and noisy memory: newsletter and promotion snippets are extracted a heartbeat after being judged junk, can publish signals, and spend extraction calls.
items.mistake: STEP-03 (c1ffbb6d) deliberately kept the old 'a judged drop is re-admitted' behaviour for archives and deferred the question to STEP-07. STEP-07 shipped without closing it, and the deploy runbook tells Harsh that archives are read by no model.
items.blocked_on: Production size (needs Rohit's permission): select attention_reason, count(*) from source_events where org_id='<ORG>' and attention_reason like 'readmitted:%' and captured_at >= '2026-10-18' group by 1;
items.verify_note: Every cited line holds. RE_ADJUDICABLE includes llm_junk (drain.py:44-49). The drain's union selects archived source_events whose event_trace reason_code is in that set and that have a payload (drain.py:159-172), then flips them to emitted/needs_extraction/P3 without running the gate (drain.py:233-247). It runs on every heartbeat with no org filter and limit 200 (routes.py:1449-1450). queue_unread files it into the re-read ladder (unread.py:338-389). to_raw_object sets rereading (unread.py:96), so whitelist returns W-06 (rules.py:326-327) and S2 is skipped (gate.py:166). The code says this is deliberate: gate.py:172-176 ('the parked drain re-admits an archived llm_junk mail exactly as it re-admitted a dropped one (03 F55)'). A confident drop keeps its light object (composio.py:615-626), and pipeline.py:1683-1686 says the archive holds 'the list snippet and headers'. One caveat: the body is whatever GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS returned in messageText (composio.py:682-684, _body_and_snippet:208). The repo has no live list response to confirm it is snippet-only.

items.title: The junk gate asks 'is a specific human writing?' but never sees who sent the mail
items.expected: The filter separates machine noise from meaningful automated or first-contact mail. Its own test is whether a named person is writing, and investors from unfamiliar domains must survive it.
items.expected_source: capture/gate/relevance.py:75-78 (the prompt's test); 05-BLUEPRINT Part 6 golden matrix 'Filtering: machine noise, meaningful automated alerts'; memory founder-workstreams-lost-2026-10-05 (Khushi/247VC, Troy/a16z S2-junked)
items.actual: The batch path sends only the masked subject plus the snippet, cut to 600 chars (relevance.py:279-286). The single path sends prepared.clean_text, which is subject plus body (pipeline.py:1622-1626; relevance.py:339). The only SOURCE line is the source name, e.g. 'gmail' (relevance.py:108). There is no sender name or domain, no 'reply to our mail' flag, and no attachment flag. Known and brief-named senders skip the gate (W-01/W-07), but a stranger is judged blind. Golden F18 (a fund's round notice) is still archived at the gate after B2.
evidence: tests/replays/specs/founder/F18.json blocked_on ('the fund's round notice is archived at the gate')
items.fix: Give each fenced item the sender's display name and domain (not the full address), an is-reply-to-us flag (from In-Reply-To/References against our sent ids) and has_attachment. Re-record the gate cassettes, and measure in the B1 live pass before relying on it.
items.effect_on_cards: First-contact investor, accelerator or fund mail can be archived. It then reaches L3 as metadata only (no words, no correlation), so no card appears.
items.verify_note: Batch path: masked subject plus snippet, cut to 600 chars (relevance.py:282-286). Single path: prepared.clean_text cut to 1500 chars (relevance.py:339). The only SOURCE line is in the single prompt (relevance.py:108); the batch prompt has none. Neither prompt carries a sender, domain, reply flag or attachment flag. W-01 known senders return keep before any call (relevance.py:329-330), and W-07 skips S2 (gate.py:166). F18 still fails: the re-recorded cassette after 0d5939d1 still holds disposition 'drop' (tests/replays/specs/founder/cassettes/F18.json), and F18.json blocked_on still says 'archived at the gate'.

items.title: No Layer 1 model site has been measured on a real model; the B2 prompt change shipped on ideal-reader answers
items.expected: Before the junk prompt changes, a live pass measures junk_gate_batch, relevance and extraction on Haiku (≈$1). Blueprint Phase 5 runs the five benchmark prompts against the actual source enumeration. A model's own confidence is never ground truth.
items.expected_source: GeniOS-008/layer-1-enterprise-signals/02-PLAN.md B1, B2 ('⛔ after B1'), R1; YC-II W27 06 D29; 05-BLUEPRINT Part 6 Phase 5
items.actual: 0d5939d1 (19 Oct) changed the gate prompt (B2 + E9), and its message says 24 gate answers were re-authored and every cassette re-recorded with the ideal reader at no spend. scripts/golden_eval.py:66 writes live scorecards to 'speedrun008/YC-II W27/scores', and that directory does not exist. The only real-model pass was the 12 Oct Haiku run on the expert site (F5). RESCUE_AT 0.70 and DROP_BELOW_RELEVANCE 0.25 (relevance.py:17,23) are unmeasured.
items.fix: Rohit sets GENIOS_GOLDEN_LIVE_KEY and says yes. Claude runs golden_eval.py --live for --site junk_gate_batch, relevance and extraction (Haiku, ≈$1, after testing 1–2 calls first), compares each case with what it needs, and tunes RESCUE_AT and the prompt from that measurement.
items.effect_on_cards: We cannot say how often the real model archives an investor, intro or portal mail, which is the top suspect for 'fewer cards'.

items.title: A failed or refused per-message Gmail fetch silently falls back to the list snippet
items.expected: A provider that says no is never read as an answer (A1's rule). A partial fetch is recorded, and a body we did not get is never passed off as the body.
items.expected_source: 02-PLAN A1; composio_base.ProviderRefused docstring (composio_base.py:12-22); 05-BLUEPRINT Part 7 'Negative-result honesty', Part 6 'Ingestion: partial fetch'
items.actual: fetch_content calls _execute without raise_if_refused (composio.py:354-355). _full_message turns every exception into {} (composio.py:358-366), and _to_objects uses `src = full or m` (composio.py:696-697), so the list message's text or snippet becomes raw['body'] with no marker. The Gmail connector's _execute also has no hard deadline, unlike ComposioExec (composio.py:309-322 vs composio_base.py:63-77). A1 guarded only the list call (composio.py:334) and the shared executor (composio_base.py:74).
items.fix: Apply raise_if_refused in fetch_content. When a keeper's full fetch fails, retry once. If it still fails, park the mail as NEEDS_REFETCH (or mark raw['body_fetch']='failed' so extraction refuses it) instead of extracting the snippet. Count it in SyncSummary and l1_sync_runs. Test plus mutation.
items.effect_on_cards: Cards built on two lines of preview, with nothing in the trace saying why.
items.mistake: A1 (e0996e6c) fixed the list call and the shared executor but not the per-message fetch, the third Composio door.
items.verify_note: fetch_content calls _execute with no raise_if_refused (composio.py:354-355). _full_message turns any exception into {} (composio.py:358-366), and a refusal envelope {successful:false,data:{}} also yields {} through r.get('data', r). The fallback is src = full or m (composio.py:697), and _body_and_snippet uses the list messageText or preview (composio.py:208). No marker is written into raw. raise_if_refused guards only the list call (composio.py:334) and ComposioExec.execute (composio_base.py:74). One detail to add: the Gmail client does have an httpx timeout=60 (composio.py:306-311). What it lacks is the 90 s executor deadline (composio_base.py:9, 63-77).

items.title: Entity doubt is thrown away, and a person known only by name never joins a bundle (E3)
items.expected: Entity resolution keeps its doubt ('probably the same person' stays probable). Correlation covers same person, similar names and uncertain matches.
items.actual: CanonicalHint.alternatives is computed, but apply_to writes only canonical_hint (validate/canonical.py:530-544). G6 (0d5939d1) keeps name-only people as unresolved candidates on the bundle (bundle.py:84-117), which is partial. L1's canonicalizer is a small alias table, so most people carry no hint and person joins by proximity effectively never fire.
items.fix: Carry the alternatives and their basis on the mention, and read them where L3 or L2 resolves identity (built with the L3 identity work, so the field has a reader).
items.effect_on_cards: Contributes to 'no correlation': two mails about one person in different threads arrive at L2 as unrelated.
items.correction: 'Doubt is thrown away' holds: apply_to writes only canonical_hint and drops alternatives (canonical.py:532-544). The mechanism behind the person-join claim is wrong. (1) Most people do carry a hint. On a miss in the alias table, propose_canonical gives a PERSON a NORMALISED_FORM hint equal to the normalised name (canonical.py:600-604; platform/identity.py:133-143), and the extractor applies it to every mention (extractor.py:1645). Measured: 'Priya' gets hint 'priya'. So G6.3's 'no canonical hint' test (bundle.py:93-99, 106-112) would almost never mark a person as name-only. (2) Proximity joins never fire for any entity, people or companies, because bundle.py reads extraction.entities while the field is entity_mentions (extraction.py:639). Measured: entity_keys() returns frozenset() on a real ExtractionResult. G6's name-only candidates and entity links are therefore never produced in production, and G6 is effectively unbuilt rather than partial.
items.verify_note: Fixing the attribute name alone would then join people on a bare name hint ('priya'), which is exactly what G6.3 meant to forbid. The hint basis needs to travel too.

items.title: Up to six producers can make a card today, each with its own switch; the L2 judgment is off by default
items.expected: One path: L1 bundle → L2 judgment (ReasoningResult) → L3 admits → L4 → L5 card. The new path is built beside the old one and switched per situation type once the golden set says it is at least as good; the formula reasoners, the LLM decider and the per-pack rule lane then retire.
items.actual: Traced from api/routes._run_l2_chain (routes.py:738): process_pending (L3 forms situations first, :799) → reason/runner.run_all (:823) → deliver.build_cards_for_org (:844) → post passes (:854). Producers and their switches: (1) the legacy per-pack rule lane, run() for every tenant_packs pack in state active/shadow (runner.py:1958-1959). Default packs are sales, general, admin and customer_support (packs/wiring.py:30-31), so it is always on. (2) The compiled L3 lane, domain_shadow.shadow_compile (runner.py:1925): L3 situation → ExpertisePackage → deterministic R-units → DecisionMaker. It is entered if the global use_domain_compiler is set, an l3_activation row exists (Admin default_on: true in Domain Expertise/Admin Expertise/domain.yaml:50; Founder Office default_on: false) or the L1 seam is on. Each situation is live only when its domain is activated (domain_shadow.py:968-995). (3) The LLM decision maker inside DecisionMaker.decide for lanes 1–2 (decision_maker.py:1120-1126). It is switched by the env vars GENIOS_L4_LLM_DECISION_MAKER and _ORGS (platform/config.py:110-111), and any failure DEFERs (llm_decision_maker.py:20-22). (4) The expert R-7 file review → covered → _decide_covered_files → signal expert.file_review, plus the founder-question card (runner.py:1901; domain_shadow.py:712-868). Switch: l4 `expert_review`, not default-on (platform/intelligence_onboarding.py:183-187). (5) The L2 R-9 judgment → written as the file's review → same path as (4) (reason/l2/sweep.py:332, 381-384). Switches: `l2_cards` + `l2_reasoning` + `expert_review` (l4_activation.py:117-127, 197-200), file subjects only, and no admission HOLD. (6) Post passes team/verify/meetings, which make deterministic cards with no switch (reason/team/postpass.py:26-30). Not producers: `situation_reasoner` R-6 is retired and its switch is refused (l4_activation.py:153-163); `cards_from_situations` only regroups what lanes 1–5 made and is off by default (intelligence_onboarding.py:172-177); `l2_reasoning` without `l2_cards` is shadow only (runner.py:1903-1910). Narration (`bundle`, R-2, default-on) changes words, never whether a card exists.
items.fix: Make the L2 judgment the one producer, one situation type at a time (I2). Write the active producer on every card (capability_key already exists) and count per producer on the funnel. Retire lanes 1–3 per type at cutover (H1–H3).
items.blocked_on: Production state not read. Rohit to run (read-only): select org_id, feature, enabled_at, disabled_at from l4_activation where feature in ('expert_review','l2_reasoning','l2_cards','cards_from_situations','bundle') order by 1,2; select org_id, domain, enabled_at, disabled_at from l3_activation order by 1,2; select capability_key, builder_version, output_lane, count(*) from cards where org_id='<ORG>' and created_at >= '2026-10-18' group by 1,2,3 order by 4 desc; plus Harsh: the value of GENIOS_L4_LLM_DECISION_MAKER(_ORGS) in the prod environment.
items.effect_on_cards: Cards come from up to six producers with different rules and voices: formula/pack cards, expert file cards, question cards and deterministic team/verify cards. Rohit cannot tell which made a card, and the mixture reads as 'weird'.
items.correction: Substance holds: six producers exist and the L2 judgment is off by default. One detail is wrong. Producer (5), the L2 R-9 card path, does not need expert_review in code. l2_pass checks only l2_reasoning (reason/l2/sweep.py:177-178) and l2_cards (makes_cards, sweep.py:335). When those two are on, a file judged through its own bundles is written as a review and covered (sweep.py:381-384, 431-433), and the compiled lane decides it. expert_review adds only two things: it hands over the moved files (to_l2_files, reason/expert/sweep.py:277-286), and it covers files from reviews that already stand. PRECONDITIONS lists expert_review (l4_activation.py:196-201), but that list is not enforced (l4_activation.py:164-168; activate() at :551-600 checks only names and retired features).
items.verify_note: Every other cited line checks out against the code: _run_l2_chain at routes.py:738-858, with process_pending (:799), run_all (:823), build_cards (:844) and post passes (:854). Also confirmed: the pack loop at runner.py:1958-1959 over tenant_packs active/shadow; DEFAULT_PACKS at packs/wiring.py:30-31; the shadow_compile entry at runner.py:1925; the LLM decision maker inside DecisionMaker.decide at decision_maker.py:1120-1126, which is also used by the legacy and native adapters through ReasoningOrchestrator (reason/adapters/legacy.py:19); the env switch at config.py:110-111; NOT_DEFAULT_ON at intelligence_onboarding.py:167-206; Admin default_on true (domain.yaml:50), with Sales :68, Support :93 and Founder Office :45 false. The post passes (reason/team/passes.py:21-43, reason/meetings/passes.py:375-383) read no switch.

items.title: A valid expert/L2 judgment makes no card unless L3 already filed a situation on the file in an activated domain; 'general' is dark
items.expected: L2 is primary: the situation is formed by reasoning, and L3 only remembers what L2 concluded. A judged file's next move reaches the founder.
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-008/00-ARCHITECTURE.md 'The flow' ("L2 is the primary layer … L3 only remembers")
items.actual: _decide_covered_files binds each covered file to a 'home' situation anchored on it, or to one it stood down (_FILES_HOME, domain_shadow.py:546-561). There are three silent ways to get no card. (i) No such situation: `covered_without_situation`, skipped (domain_shadow.py:741-745). (ii) The situation's L2 domain maps to no corpus. `general` → None (domain_shadow.py:952-965; DARK_DOMAINS context/domain_silence.py:45-60), so live_lane is False (domain_shadow.py:993-995) and the decision is made in SHADOW only, `expert_shadow` (domain_shadow.py:796-798). `general` is the fallback whenever no domain hint fired (context/domain_spec.py:142; :660-670 says 'most of it: 23 of one tenant's 30 deal-anchored correlations'). (iii) No tenant pack for the domain: `expert_no_tenant_pack` (domain_shadow.py:754-756). The only record of any of these is one `domain-compiler …` log line (domain_shadow.py:2054).
items.fix: Bind a covered file's decision to the file itself: its own node as subject, its pack from the file's work kind, or a founder_office/admin default for founder work. Stop requiring an L3 situation plus a mapped domain. Until then, count covered_without_situation / expert_shadow / no_tenant_pack on the funnel and log a warning. Run the 'general' census that DARK_DOMAINS names as its end condition.
items.blocked_on: How many judged files are lost this way in production. Rohit to run: select s.domain, count(distinct r.file_id) from expert_reviews r join context_situations s on s.org_id=r.org_id and s.anchor_node_id=r.file_id where r.org_id='<ORG>' and r.status='valid' and s.status in ('active','partial') group by 1; select count(distinct r.file_id) from expert_reviews r where r.org_id='<ORG>' and r.status='valid' and not exists (select 1 from context_situations s where s.org_id=r.org_id and s.anchor_node_id=r.file_id);
items.effect_on_cards: Fewer cards. The expert's or L2's best reading of a file can be stored as valid and never shown: no card and no signal, nothing Rohit can see. This is one concrete form of 'L2 and L3 failing each other'.
items.mistake: STEP-12 M33 bolted the file review onto the compiled situation lane (bind to a situation, gate by its domain) instead of giving the file its own route. That L3-first dependency is what Atlas v2 removes.
items.correction: Substance holds. The three silent no-card exits are at domain_shadow.py:741-745 (covered_without_situation), :754-756 (expert_no_tenant_pack) and :796-798 (expert_shadow when l3_domain_for('general') is None, :952-965 and :993-995). One detail is overstated: 'the only record is one log line' is true for (i) and (iii) only. For (ii), the shadow decision is also written as a change-gate row: gate.record(key, fingerprint, 'shadow', run_id) at :797, flushed to reasoning_fingerprints with lane='compiled' and outcome='shadow' (domain_shadow.py:1177-1191; fingerprint_store.py:66-82). That row does not say why the decision was shadow; the reason is only in the log line (:2054).
items.verify_note: The general fallback is at context/domain_spec.py:142 (canonical_domain → 'general'). The '23 of 30' comment is at :660-670. DARK_DOMAINS['general'] is at context/domain_silence.py:45-60. _FILES_HOME and _STOOD_DOWN_HOME are at :546-561.

items.title: Held cards read as engineer sentences: a fixed template replaces the model's advice, and nothing repairs before holding
items.expected: The card speaks in the founder's words, shows the move, and asks one clear question only when it must. The held wording is rewritten in the reader's words (GeniOS-009 G0.2.b).
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-009/STEP-G0-the-ground.md G0.2.b; 01-AS-IS-CARDS.md A2; memory dashboard-visual-style ('one clear line')
items.actual: The template is reason/expert/verify.py:787-793 `_held_question`: "What is the next step with {counterparty name or key}? We held the one we found: {why}." The `why` comes from the closed phrases in contracts/claim_check.py:131-153 HELD_BECAUSE, e.g. UNQUOTED (:134) "a fact your move rests on quotes nothing from the mail it cites", plus the four JUDGMENT_HOLDS phrases added 21 Oct (:78-82, :149-152). The card's second line is reason/expert/asks.py:69-79 WHY_*, e.g. "we could not confirm what it rests on from what it cites". question_words takes checked.question for a held file (asks.py:181-189). The model's move is deliberately withheld (verify.py:787-792 'NEVER THE WORDS THAT FAILED'; the headline is set only when shown, verify.py:1310-1316). The counterparty falls back to a bare domain ('latticecap.test'). Nothing repairs first: R-7 repairs syntax only (reason/expert/review.py:171), and R-9 repairs other failures only at deep depth (reason/l2/judge.py:115-119). A held fate never raises, only REFUSED does (judge.py:105-108), so a citation slip becomes a question to Rohit and the model never gets a second try.
items.fix: (1) Rewrite HELD_BECAUSE, _held_question and asks.WHY_* in the founder's voice, leading with the move to confirm (e.g. 'Follow up with Cobalt Peak? I couldn't find the line in their mail this rests on — confirm and I'll keep it'). Never print a bare domain as a name. (2) Before holding, make one repair call that carries the check's verdicts, at every depth and on both R-7 and R-9 (STEP-13b's repair). (3) Test with a golden headline assertion on F15 and a mutation on the template.
items.blocked_on: Share of held cards in production: select checked->>'fate' fate, checked->>'because' because, count(*) from expert_reviews where org_id='<ORG>' and reviewed_at>='2026-10-18' and status='valid' group by 1,2 order by 3 desc;
items.effect_on_cards: Weird wording: question cards whose headline is an internal check result, with no advice on them.
items.mistake: STEP-13 X10 chose closed phrases so that failed words never reach a card (right), but the phrases were written about the check, not for the founder. The L2 rebuild reused them unchanged.
items.verify_note: _held_question is at verify.py:787-793 and is used at :1239, :1242 and :1290. HELD_BECAUSE is at claim_check.py:131-153 (UNQUOTED :134, MOVE_DATE_PASSED :152), and the JUDGMENT_HOLDS reasons are at :78-82. WHY_* are at asks.py:69-79, and question_words takes checked.question for a held file at asks.py:183-189. The headline and draft are blanked unless shown (verify.py:1309-1316). R-7 runs with repair=REPAIR_SYNTAX (review.py:171), and gate.py:380-382 breaks on any refusal that is not MALFORMED. R-9 uses REPAIR_ANY only at deep depth (judge.py:115-119). Only a REFUSED fate raises SiteRejection (judge.py:105-108), so a held fate is never retried at any depth. The golden dump (measurements/golden-cards-2026-10-22.json, F15.l2.cards) shows 5 headlines in this template, one naming 'latticecap.test'.

items.title: When a judgment fails or is held, the file falls back to the formula/pack lanes; refused and truncated answers are never retried
items.expected: No formula decides meaning. A failure gives a partial result plus EvidenceNeeds, 'never a forced conclusion'. Malformed output gets one bounded repair, then a failure status.
items.actual: A file is covered only by a VALID review. A file whose review was refused (nothing stands), truncated, failed, over budget, carried past MAX_PER_PASS=10, or (under l2_cards) whose admission came back HOLD 'is decided as before, situation by situation'. That means the compiled formula lane and the per-pack rules decide it (reason/expert/sweep.py:39-50 docstring, :262-264, :296-309; reason/l2/sweep.py:378-384; reason/runner.py:1958-1959). REFUSED and TRUNCATED are STANDING statuses, so the same fingerprint is never asked again until the file moves (reason/expert/store.py:62; reason/l2/store.py:57). R-9's 8,000-token ceiling is modelled, not measured (reason/bundle/sites.py:142-146; 04-FOR-HARSH G-1 'If a row is truncated, tell me').
items.fix: Keep a file covered by its last valid review (shown 'as of <date>') when the new one fails, instead of handing it to the formula lanes. Retry a truncated answer once at a larger ceiling. Give a refused answer one repair with the verdicts. Count 'fell back' per sweep.
items.blocked_on: select status, left(reason,120) r, count(*) from expert_reviews where org_id='<ORG>' and reviewed_at>='2026-10-18' and status<>'valid' group by 1,2 order by 3 desc; select status, count(*) from reasoning_results where org_id='<ORG>' group by 1;
items.effect_on_cards: Weird cards. The same counterparty can get a formula/pack card (Admin-rule wording) in place of, or next to, the expert's file card.
items.mistake: STEP-12 D1 kept the old lanes as the fallback for any file without a valid review. That was safe for a shadow pilot, but it contradicts the L2-primary architecture.
items.verify_note: The expert sweep docstring (sweep.py:41-52) says that refused, cut, failed-waiting, carried and unreadable files are 'decided as before, situation by situation'. Code: _waiting at :124-133, OVER_BUDGET break at :304-306, and the cap of 10 at :92 and :289-291. In the L2 sweep, only an admitted or rejected result with checked becomes a review (reason/l2/sweep.py:378-384); a HOLD, or a result that never ended, writes nothing. STANDING = (VALID, REFUSED, TRUNCATED) at expert/store.py:62, and (RESULT, REFUSED, TRUNCATED) at l2/store.py:57. The 8,000-token ceiling is labelled [MODELLED] at bundle/sites.py:142-146. Uncovered files fall to shadow_compile and the pack loop (runner.py:1925-1960).

items.title: The shared 7-per-day signal cap is spent by formula situations before the expert/L2 file decisions get a turn
items.expected: The expert's judgment decides what matters; a busy day shows the nearest deadlines first.
items.expected_source: genios_engine/reason/expert/sweep.py:17-21 docstring (06 D1, D7); speedrun008/GeniOS-008/00-ARCHITECTURE.md L2 primary
items.actual: One cap covers every lane: _daily_allowance = pack budget_per_day (default 7) × active seats − every signal row of the org created today (domain_shadow.py:165-186; reason/runner.py:551-555). Inside shadow_compile, the situation loop spends it first (domain_shadow.py:1913-1944). Covered expert/L2 files are decided after the loop (domain_shadow.py:2016-2021). A spent cap drops the file's decision as `budget_exhausted` (domain_shadow.py:813-816), which appears only in the log line. Signals from earlier sweeps of the same day, from any lane, are already subtracted.
items.fix: Decide covered files before the situation loop, or give file decisions their own allowance. Count budget_exhausted on the funnel. Add a test where 7 formula situations are emitted, then 1 expert file, and the expert card must exist.
items.blocked_on: select created_at::date d, rule_id, count(*) from signals where org_id='<ORG>' and created_at>='2026-10-18' group by 1,2 order by 1,3 desc;
items.effect_on_cards: Fewer expert cards on busy days, while formula cards take their slots.
items.verify_note: _daily_allowance is budget_per_day (default 7) × _active_seats − _budget_used (domain_shadow.py:165-186). _budget_used counts every signals row of the org with created_at::date = today, whatever its lane or status (runner.py:551-555). The situation loop spends the cap first (domain_shadow.py:1912-1944), and covered files are decided after it (:2016-2021). For a file, budget_exhausted applies only to a shown move: a NO_MOVE outcome, a question, a renewal or a small move is exempt (:813). Its trace is a change-gate row with outcome 'indeterminate' (:815), so it is retried next sweep, and the reason itself appears only in the log line at :2054.

items.title: Nearly every skip, refusal, budget cap or shadow decision is invisible to Rohit and shows only in a server log line
items.expected: 'A SKIP IS A ROW', and a refusal nobody can see is a silent stop. Each pass's receipt is readable by an operator, and Rohit can tell why a file has no card.
items.actual: Skip points and where each one shows: (1) Expert not activated or no model: returns {'skipped':…} (reason/expert/sweep.py:163-176). run_all only returns it (runner.py:2011-2012) and _run_l2_chain never logs it (api/routes.py:822-823). (2) Expert cap of 10 a pass and $2/day at $0.10/call (sweep.py:92, 296-309; reason/bundle/budget.py:63-64), failed-waits-6h and over-budget-waits-a-day (sweep.py:96, 140-149). These are logged only when something was reviewed or carried (sweep.py:324-325). (3) Refused and truncated reviews stand (store.py:62). (4) L2 not activated or no model (reason/l2/sweep.py:177-181) is never logged. The L2 cap of 10 at $2/day and $0.15/call (sweep.py:62, 296-300; budget.py:68-71) is logged only when rows or carried exist (sweep.py:443-444). (5) Covered-file outcomes covered_without_situation, expert_no_tenant_pack, expert_shadow, budget_exhausted and expert_small_move (domain_shadow.py:744, 755, 797, 815, 824) appear in one 'domain-compiler' log line (domain_shadow.py:2054). (6) R-site ledger rows exist for every consult outcome (l4_r_site_calls; sites.py:181-207). Operator surfaces: scripts/pipeline_health.py reads expert_reviews (:925-975) but not reasoning_results or R-9; scripts/l2_shadow_report.py; the funnel has five stages and none for judged/held/refused/fell-back (platform/funnel.py:60-61). No API route reads expert_reviews, reasoning_results or l4_r_site_calls except the erasure lists (api/account_routes.py:662, 683, 940). Rohit sees only the held question card.
items.fix: Add funnel counts written by run_all: judged, held, refused, truncated, carried_budget, fell_back, covered_not_carded, budget_exhausted. Always log the expert/L2 'skipped' reason. Add R-9/reasoning_results to pipeline_health. Add one admin route plus a 'why no card' line on the file page.
items.effect_on_cards: Silent stops: when cards drop, neither Rohit nor an operator can see which gate dropped them without reading server logs.
items.mistake: Each unit added its own counter to its own receipt, and none was relayed to the funnel or to a surface.
items.correction: Substance holds: the skips, caps, refusals and shadow outcomes are not visible to Rohit on any surface he uses. One detail is wrong: an API route does read expert_reviews. GET /v1/workstreams/{file_id} returns the file's latest STANDING review (valid, refused or truncated, with its reason, model, cost, check fate, question and verdicts) and its latest valid review (api/workstream_routes.py:153-167, reading reason/expert/store). The dashboard does not call it: git grep for 'workstream' at dashboard origin/main 2edfb86 returns 0 hits. reasoning_results, l2_admissions and l4_r_site_calls are still read by no route except the erasure lists (account_routes.py:662, 683, 940, 942).
items.verify_note: Also confirmed: expert_pass returns {'skipped':…} at sweep.py:163-176, and run_all only returns it (runner.py:2011-2012); routes.py:822-823 never logs it, and stage() logs only timing. Under l2_cards the expert pass returns at :270-277, before its only log line (:324-325), so its receipt is never logged. The L2 skips at l2/sweep.py:175-181 are unlogged, and the L2 log fires only if rows or carried (:443-444). The funnel has five closed stages (platform/funnel.py:55-61). pipeline_health.py reads expert_reviews and R-7's l4_r_site_calls (:925-975) but not reasoning_results.

items.title: With l2_cards on but l2_reasoning off (or no R-9 client), nobody judges a moved file
items.expected: l2_cards requires l2_reasoning and expert_review: the pass that judges, and the review path its result decides through.
items.actual: PRECONDITIONS are 'NOT enforced … REPORTED' (l4_activation.py:166-170). expert_pass sees l2_cards, builds no R-7 client and hands every moved file to L2 (reason/expert/sweep.py:171-176, 277-286). l2_pass then returns {'skipped': 'l2_reasoning_not_activated'} or 'no_model_configured' (reason/l2/sweep.py:177-181), and neither is logged. Moved files lose cover and fall to the formula lanes.
items.fix: In expert_pass, set l2_judges = l2_cards AND l2_reasoning AND a buildable R-9 client. Otherwise the expert reviews as before and logs a warning. Add a test with l2_cards on and l2_reasoning off where R-7 must still run.
items.blocked_on: Whether production is in this state: select org_id, feature, disabled_at from l4_activation where feature in ('l2_cards','l2_reasoning','expert_review');
items.effect_on_cards: Silent stop: no new file judgments, and only stale or formula cards. This is latent until the switches are mismatched.
items.verify_note: PRECONDITIONS is 'NOT enforced … REPORTED' (l4_activation.py:164-168), and activate() (:551-600) checks only require_feature and RETIRED_FEATURES. Under l2_cards, expert_pass builds no client and returns to_l2_files (expert/sweep.py:171-176, 270-277). l2_pass then returns {'skipped': 'l2_reasoning_not_activated'} or 'no_model_configured' (l2/sweep.py:177-181) without logging. The moved files were never covered (they were appended to due, not _cover'ed), so they fall to the formula lanes. The reverse failure is also unenforced: with l2_cards and l2_reasoning on but expert_review off, the expert pass skips, so standing reviews are not covered and moved files are not handed over. Only bundle-touched files are judged.

items.title: A subject with no file (a first mail, a new admission) is judged but can never become a card
items.expected: The subject is the file when one exists, else the seed thread/entity (L2-Q6). L2 forms the situation and L3 admits it.
items.actual: Seed subjects are read and judged with the brief as block D (reason/l2/sweep.py:210-219, 338-341; reason/l2/dossier.py:169-172). Only file subjects are written as a review that can make a card (reason/l2/sweep.py:381: `parts is not None`). A seed's `create` proposal is HOLD at subject level, 'no situation seed for this subject yet — no join has filed it' (context/l2_admission.py:97-102). There is no applier and no EvidenceNeed.
items.fix: Build an L3 applier for an admitted `create` on a seed (GeniOS-009 G0.3, one type first), and a card path for a seed's result (subject = the thread's counterparty node).
items.effect_on_cards: Fewer cards. New work that no file or situation yet holds (e.g. the Antler Singapore admission thread) cannot get an L2 card.
items.verify_note: A seed subject gets brief_block in place of a file dossier (l2/sweep.py:335-338; l2/dossier.py:167-172, which says 'No file holds this subject … judge from the brief'). A review is written only if parts is not None (l2/sweep.py:381). A seed create becomes HOLD with NO_SITUATION and the reason 'no situation seed for this subject yet — no join has filed it' (context/l2_admission.py:97-102). Nothing reads that HOLD. needs_from may still file the result's own evidence needs (l2/sweep.py:364-366), but no need is raised for the hold itself.

items.title: Under l2_cards the judgment half (six-dimension confidence, options, decision need, history) is dropped; the card still shows formula {C,U,I} (L2-9)
items.expected: A lane plus a six-dimension confidence vector (evidence · frame · temporal · causal · authority · coverage), each a level with its reason, and no single scalar floor. The card shows options, decision need and authority.
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-008/00-ARCHITECTURE.md 'Cards — five lanes, a confidence vector'; 02-MIGRATION-PLAN.md:140 L2-9; GeniOS-009 STEP-G6 §5
items.actual: L2Judgment carries the six dimensions, options, decision_need, history_used and second_order (contracts/reasoning_result.py:73-75, 227-238). When an L2 result becomes the file's review, only result.review and result.checked are written (reason/l2/sweep.py:121-139). write_review has no judgment field (reason/expert/store.py:194-199). decide and the card never see the judgment half; it lives only in reasoning_results. The card's confidence_vector comes from the formula's C/U/I/R SQL (deliver/card_builder.py:1369-1370; reason/authority.py:105-115). The expert decision's confidence is code counting cited events, with a 6,000 bp scalar floor and 4,000 bp below it (reason/expert/decide.py:41-49, 170-172). Golden: 49/57 cards carry {C,I,U} (01-AS-IS-CARDS §2). The key names also differ: code uses 'framing' (reasoning_result.py:73) where Atlas and G6 say 'frame'.
items.fix: Carry the judgment half to the card: store it with the review row, or join reasoning_results by fingerprint in decide. Render the six named levels with reasons, options and decision need. Drop the scalar floor for L2 cards (the lane already encodes it). Align the key 'framing' vs 'frame'.
items.effect_on_cards: Confidence on the card is an opaque formula number. The L2 reasoning Rohit was promised (options, who decides, history) never appears.
items.mistake: L2 rebuild C1 (de795bb8) reused the expert review row as the hand-off and wrote only the review half.
items.correction: Substance holds: under l2_cards the review row has no judgment field (expert/store.py:194-199), and _file_review copies only result.review and result.checked (l2/sweep.py:121-139). The card shows the formula C/U/I (card_builder.py:1369-1370; authority.py:105-115), and the expert confidence is the event-count floor (decide.py:41-49, 168-172). Two details are wrong. (1) 'decide and the card never see the judgment half' is false since 9794dfec (21 Oct): lane_for (computed from evidence and framing confidence, open_conflict) and decision_need/by_when reach the card through judgment_hold. That turns the move into a held question (judge.py:102-104; reasoning_result.py:447-480; verify.py:1287-1293). (2) 'it lives only in reasoning_results' is false: since f3cfd3c6 (20 Oct) an admitted judgment's frame, intervention_mode and decision object are appended to situation_interpretations (context/l2_admission.py:141-201). Nothing reads that table. The six dimensions, options and history_used still reach no card.
items.verify_note: The naming mismatch holds: the code uses 'framing' (reasoning_result.py:73), while 00-ARCHITECTURE.md:114 and STEP-G6 :63 say 'frame'. 01-AS-IS-CARDS.md:43 says 49/57 cards carry {C,I,U}.

items.title: Since 21 Oct an overdue move, an 'unknown' confidence or an unnamed decider turns the move into a held question
items.expected: Uncertainty routes a finding to a lane; it never deletes it. review_required means a person looks first, not that the advice is withheld.
items.actual: judgment_hold (contracts/reasoning_result.py:462-480, added in 9794dfec on 21 Oct, on the production head) holds an act's move as one question in four cases: the move's by_when is before the run (MOVE_IN_THE_PAST, :396-398); a decision is needed and nobody is named (:392-393); evidence or framing confidence is low or 'unknown' (lane_for → monitor, :447-459); or a conflict is open. The prompt itself says 'Unknown is an answer when it is said why' (reason/l2/prompt.py:57-59). verify.py:1288-1293 then produces 'What is the next step with X? We held the one we found: the date the move was for has already passed.'
items.fix: Show an overdue move as overdue, re-dated to today. Show weak ground as a monitor card that keeps the move as a 'watch'. For a solo-founder tenant, default the decider to 'you'. Hold only an open conflict.

A file has a work_kind only if an accepted brief in_motion line names its address or domain (context/workstreams.py:19-25, 298-310). 'partner' maps to no capability (packs/compiler/playbook_reader.py:48-55). Seeds get only the brief (reason/l2/dossier.py:169-172). items.correction: Substance holds: reason/l2 imports nothing from packs/ (grep returns 0). The expertise is the expert dossier's playbook section, chosen by work_kind (expert/dossier.py:495-546, 772-784). work_kind comes only from an in_motion brief line (context/workstreams.py:298-310). Seeds get the brief only (l2/dossier.py:167-172), comparable() returns nothing without a kind (l2/history.py:43-47), and expertise_ref hashes the dossier digest + brief + prompt (l2/sweep.py:339-340). It is not 'one Founder Office playbook': KIND_CAPABILITY maps 6 of the 7 kinds, 5 to Founder Office capabilities and 'vendor' to admin.contract_and_vendor.renewal_management (packs/compiler/playbook_reader.py:48-56), with only 'partner' → None. items.fix: In reason/l2/sweep.py, when a file review is written, call propose_kind if result.review.proposed_kind stands the check. Test that a file with a proposed kind gets a brief proposal under l2_cards.

items.verify_note: propose_kind's only caller is reason/expert/sweep.py:310-321, after an R-7 call. Under l2_cards the pass returns at :270-277 before that point. An ADMIT flips a seed to active, a REJECT archives it with resolved_by='admission', and a HOLD keeps it a seed with its reason. The card source reads only admitted rows. Merge the two doors into one: have situation_publisher take L2's proposal, or retire it.

Neither door decides whether a row exists. But 'gate nothing' is wrong for both doors. That review is the file's card source and covers it (reason/l2/sweep.py:376-383). So each door gates downstream reasoning or cards; neither gates existence.

Either store the counterparty/file node beside the synthetic anchor (finding.concerns_node already exists) and include those rows in lifecycle_for and decide(), or move the readings into L2 as inputs (L2-11). items.title: One counterparty file holds many live situations (one per keyword domain × 45-day generation, plus readings), so the L2 judgment is HELD instead of admitted
items.expected: One situation per subject; a card is a living view of one situation (versions, not new pings).
items.actual: The correlation key is (anchor node, domain, generation). The domain is chosen per message: the L1 keyword hint, otherwise the gate's fallback 'admin' for every emitted mail with no keyword. So an invite titled 'Theresa <> Rohit' and an email that says 'investor', both with the same company, open two correlations, and refresh_situations writes one situation per correlation. A file unions them (workstreams), but decide() HOLDs 'one of several live situations, and the judgment named none of them'. With l2_cards on, a HOLD file gets no L2 file review and no R-7 call, so its cards come from the old lane.
evidence: genios_engine/context/correlation.py:175 (base_key = node + domain), :426-456 (find_or_open by anchor+domain, new generation after the window), :76 CORRELATION_WINDOW_DAYS = 45
genios_engine/reason/l2/sweep.py:381-383 (no file review on HOLD); genios_engine/reason/expert/sweep.py:168-175 (no R-7 call with l2_cards)
items.fix: Make the subject the unit: one live situation per file, with the domain as an attribute and not part of the key, or a file-level admission that names a primary situation. Let the judgment cite sit:<id>, since the dossier already prints it. Close the generation split for kinds with a declared window. Measure with the SQL first.
items.blocked_on: Production read (Rohit's permission): select anchor_node_id, count(*) filter (where status in ('active','partial')) as live, array_agg(distinct domain) as domains, array_agg(distinct situation_type) as types from context_situations where org_id='<rohit_org>' group by anchor_node_id having count(*) filter (where status in ('active','partial')) > 1 order by live desc limit 30;
items.effect_on_cards: Duplicate or split cards for one counterparty. The L2 judgment's conclusion is never admitted, and the old lane's card stands instead.
items.correction: The mechanism holds. The key is node + domain + generation (correlation.py:173-175, :426-456). The domain is per message, with an 'admin' fallback (hints.py:78, capture/pipeline.py:1670-1671). refresh_situations writes one row per correlation (situations.py:1178-1222). The HOLD path is at l2_admission.py:112-116 and sweep.py:381-382. The expert pass makes no R-7 call under l2_cards (expert/sweep.py:166-171). Two details are wrong. (1) Generations add little to the LIVE count. An old generation goes dormant at DORMANT_AFTER_DAYS=45 (situations.py:87), the same clock that opens the next one. The window is also not always 45 days: a file's kind can stretch it, e.g. investor or program to 90 days via file_quiet_days (correlation.py:395-413, :437-438). So live multiplicity comes mainly from domains. (2) It is worse than stated. When the judgment names ONE of several live situations, every other live unnamed one is still HOLD (l2_admission.py:99-116, the else branch). Any HOLD blocks the file review (sweep.py:381-382). So a file with two or more live situations gets an L2 file review only when the judgment names all of them or proposes create.
items.verify_note: With l2_cards on, the expert pass still answers from standing reviews (expert/sweep.py:166-169). A file that moved has a new fingerprint, so in practice its cards fall back to the old lane, as the item says.

items.title: Thread inheritance reads reading-declared memberships: a reply can join a reading's synthetic correlation and no file, and the backfill and the 'filed' health check count those events as filed
items.expected: Under-correlate rather than over-correlate, but never lose an event from its conversation. Only the correlation engine owns membership of real correlations.
items.expected_source: genios_engine/context/correlation.py:1-50 (module law); genios_engine/context/correlation_membership.py:92-98 ('a reading only claims its own correlation')
items.actual: Readings write context_correlation_members rows under synthetic ids (joined_via='reading'). thread_correlations returns every correlation id with a member in the thread and does not check that a context_correlations row owns it. If that list has one id, _the_parties_files returns it unchanged and the new event joins only that id. The id is synthetic, so the event is in no file, because files join context_correlations. If the list has several ids and the reply touches none of their anchors, the reply also joins every reading correlation. The non-rebuild backfill skips any event already in context_correlation_members, and _NAMED_MAIL counts any membership as 'filed'.
evidence: genios_engine/context/correlation_membership.py:126-130 (insert members, joined_via 'reading'); callers outreach_situations.py:1875, support_situations.py:1606, meeting_touch.py:243, document_register.py:580
genios_engine/context/correlation.py:358-363 (no ownership/joined_via filter), :592-599 (one id returned as-is; none touched keeps all), :632-638 (joins inherited ids only)
genios_engine/context/workstreams.py:162-169 (_MEMBERS joins context_correlations: synthetic ids are no file)
items.fix: In thread_correlations, the backfill skip and _NAMED_MAIL, count only engine-owned ids: join context_correlations, or filter joined_via <> 'reading'. Add a PG test where a reading declared the only earlier event of a thread and assert that the reply joins the counterparty's file.

items.effect_on_cards: A reply that belongs in an investor's file lands in none, and L2 judges it as a contextless seed ('no correlation').
items.mistake: The declare_finding_events wiring (added to feed gather_l1_signals) put reading rows into the table that thread inheritance reads as conversation identity. This is the 'absence was the only guard' family.
items.verify_note: Verified. declare_finding_events inserts members with joined_via='reading', and only for ids no context_correlations row owns (correlation_membership.py:116-130). thread_correlations has no ownership or joined_via filter (correlation.py:358-363). _the_parties_files returns a single id unchanged (:578-579). With several ids, it keeps every id, reading ids included, when no owned anchor was touched (:580-585). Every inherited id gets a member (:632-638). _MEMBERS joins context_correlations, so synthetic ids are no file (workstreams.py:162-169). The backfill skips any event that is already a member (backfill.py:~141-142). _NAMED_MAIL counts any membership as filed (workstreams.py:230-233).

items.title: L2 subjects come from L1 bundles matched to L3 files by event: an unfiled bundle becomes a contextless 'seed' whose HOLD dead-ends, the watermark passes it, and a bundle spanning two files is judged under the first only
items.expected: Correlation happens before reasoning. L2 reads a bounded snapshot of what the company knows, and a HOLD raises an EvidenceNeed so the gap is fetched.
items.actual: subjects_for takes files[0] of a bundle's files, sorted by node id, and ignores the rest. With no file the bundle becomes 'seed:<thread>'. decide() on a seed proposing create returns HOLD with situation '-' ('no join has filed it'). No code mints the row later, and the HOLD raises no EvidenceNeed. The seed's snapshot seeds are the nodes its events wrote facts on, at most 5; if there are none the snapshot is EMPTY. The pass then advances its watermark past judged seeds (only unreached subjects hold it back). An event that is filed a sweep later is not re-judged under its file from that bundle.
items.fix: Re-key a seed subject to its file once its events are filed (a re-entry when an event joins a file). Judge a multi-file bundle under each file. Give HOLD '-' either an applier or an EvidenceNeed. Count seed subjects and empty snapshots in the pass receipt.
items.blocked_on: Production read: select (subject_ref like 'seed:%') as seed, status, lane, count(*) from reasoning_results where org_id='<rohit_org>' and reasoned_at > now() - interval '7 days' group by 1,2,3;
items.effect_on_cards: 'Sometimes no correlation': the judgment sees a thread with no file, history or people. No card results, or a context-free one.
items.verify_note: Verified. subjects_for takes files[0] of a sorted set; with no file the subject is seed:<thread or subject> (reason/l2/inputs.py:177-184). file_of_event is a dict, so an event in two files keeps only one (inputs.py:216). A seed has no parts, so decide() returns HOLD '-' when it proposes create (l2_admission.py:94-98). Snapshot seeds are at most 5 fact-subject nodes, and there is EMPTY when none (snapshot.py:24-30, :62-76). The watermark is held back only by unreached, unreadable, waiting, too-big or carried subjects (sweep.py:353-356, :398-416). The HOLD itself raises no need. Needs the model's result asks for ARE still filed (sweep.py:356-358, evidence.needs_from), and settled needs re-enter through evidence.reentries (sweep.py:212-217).

items.title: l2_admissions is shadow only: written only when l2_reasoning is on, read by nothing, HOLDs have no applier, merge/link have no applier
items.expected: L3 admission decides existence (ADMIT/HOLD/REJECT); HOLD raises an EvidenceNeed; card path reads admitted situations (Phase C).
items.actual: The L2 pass returns before any read when l2_reasoning is not activated, and the feature is off by default. The admission write happens inside a savepoint, so a failure only sets receipt['admissions_failed']. admitted() has no caller. merge and link proposals are always HOLD ('no applier yet'). Only the latest decision per (subject, situation) is kept, keyed by situation ids that a rebuild re-mints.
items.fix: After l3-admission-cannot-see-reading-situations and G0.3: make admitted() the card source for the first type, build merge and link appliers, and add the HOLD→EvidenceNeed link. Until then, report admission counts in the sweep or funnel so the shadow can be read.

items.correction: The table claims hold. The pass returns before any read when l2_reasoning is off (sweep.py:176-178). l2_reasoning and l2_cards are in NOT_DEFAULT_ON (intelligence_onboarding.py:193-203). The write is in a savepoint and failure sets admissions_failed (sweep.py:421-429). merge and link are always HOLD (l2_admission.py:49, :104-105).
