items.title: Rohit's binding card contract vs what GET /cards and GET /cards/{id} return, field by field
items.expected: Face: a subject that is a clear action, then 1–2 lines on what to do and how. Opened: the recommendation; what · why · how; what doing it gets you; the goal it moves; the deadline; the details; where the data came from. Every card's details are its own and never repeated across cards.
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-010/06-CARDS/README.md 'What Rohit asked' round 5; 02-CARD-DEFINITION.md §2–§3; memory cards-ux-analysis-22-oct.md 'Round 3: his card contract (binding)'
items.actual:
GET /cards returns 13 fields per row: card_id, signal_id, assignee, domain, urgency_band, headline, subject_node_id, situation, score, state, render_mode, created_at, expires_at (plus your_part for a seat). It does not return recommended, output_lane, why_now, actions, context_tags, version or by_when.

GET /cards/{id} returns k.* plus three more columns, context, actionability, decision, actions and screen_items. Field by field:
- Subject = headline. Clarity is not guaranteed; see l5-subject-writer.
- Two lines = recommended.what, on expert/L2 cards only; formula cards have only the projection.
- Recommendation = recommended{who,what,for_whom,by_when} plus decision.recommendation. The projection's steps are empty on expert cards (the play has no steps) and stock on formula cards.
- What = situation (the expert's reading, labelled an inference).
- Why = why_now / unresolved_item.
- How = steps (see above).
- What it gets you = success_signal (expert: done_when from the play's success_events; formula: the play's stock line) plus do_nothing_consequence. scenarios.act is absent.
- Goal: no field exists.
- Deadline = recommended.by_when, outcome_window_days, and the person-level commitments[].due_at.
- Details = business_subject, relationship_role, why[] (bare quote strings) and person-level context.
- Where the data came from = context_tags plus why[].source. This works.
- Own details: violated by person-level context and stock sentences.
evidence: genios_engine/deliver/store.py:658-690 (get_authoritative_card selects k.* + candidate_steps, rejected_candidates, decision_uncertainty)
dashboard origin/main src/app/dashboard/cards/page.tsx:925 (Goal row hard-coded 'Not linked to a goal yet')
items.fix: Build C6 → C2 → C1 → C4 → C3 → C5 → C7 → C8 in that order (01-INTEGRATION §5). Each is listed as its own item below.
items.effect_on_cards: Cards read as a kind of card rather than this situation: unclear subjects, empty or stock How, a result that is often stock, no goal, and the same details on several cards.
items.correction: One detail is wrong: the reason expert steps are empty. The expert play does have a step. decide.py:287 builds MOVE_PLAY with steps=(words.headline,), and decision_maker.py:898 copies play.steps into the candidate parameters. The step is lost because the compiled/expert signal insert (reason/domain_shadow.py:343-357) never writes signals.candidate_steps; only the legacy runner path writes it (runner.py:806 via _decision_payload). So get_card's s.candidate_steps is NULL, and _decision_projection (routes.py:5118-5128) gets no decided_steps. On an actionable expert card it drops to the else branch with steps=[]. On a non-actionable card it uses the stock line 'Open the source and review the request'.
items.verify_note: Everything else holds. The three queue SELECTs project exactly 13 columns (store.py:772-787). _your_part adds your_part (store.py:984). get_authoritative_card selects k.* plus candidate_steps, rejected_candidates and decision_uncertainty (store.py:658-660). get_card adds context, actionability, decision, actions and screen_items (routes.py:5567-5603). No goal column exists in the cards insert (store.py:446-467). Dashboard origin/main page.tsx:925 hard-codes 'Not linked to a goal yet'.

items.title: No card writer (C1): the subject is a clause cut of the model's move, a pack template, or the l5_render line; garbled headlines come from this chain
items.expected: The subject starts with a verb, is at most about 10 words, names the person or thing, and is never a cut sentence or placeholder ("…to body"). It is written once per card version by deliver/card_copy.py into cards.copy, and every sentence is checked.
items.actual:
deliver/card_copy.py and a cards.copy column do not exist. Headlines have four writers:
1. Expert/L2 cards: reason/expert/decide._render puts the model's checked headline (words.headline) into fallback.headline. card_builder._gold_template then applies gold_headline(), which cuts to HEADLINE_CAP=60 at _GOLD_CUT. That pattern splits before 'to', 'with', 'for', 'on', 'in' and similar words, which start phrases, not clauses. render._fallback re-caps it, and pipeline.py:1003 state_not_command adds 'Needs a decision — ' / 'Unresolved — ' to review- and observation-level cards. That leaves 41 characters for the body, which _cap fits by sentence, then clause, then word.
2. Formula cards: render.render_copy (model site l5_render, max_tokens=600), trimmed by _fit/_fit_clauses, or on failure the pack template, e.g. packs/general_v1.py:174 'Deliver {action} to {entity} today'.
3. Question cards: the model's question text.
4. executive_bridge reminders: '{frame} — {goal}'.
The phrase 'Send calendar invites with meeting link to body' is not in the repo. Without the production row I cannot tell which of writers 1–3 produced it.
evidence: genios_engine/deliver/pipeline.py:980-1003 (render_copy with llm=None for expert; then state_not_command)
items.fix: Build C1 as specified: deliver/card_copy.py, called after build_draft and the claim check, once per new card version and never per view. It writes subject, summary, steps, result and goal, each with rests_on, and a sentence that rests on nothing is dropped. Add a migration for cards.copy jsonb, serve copy.subject and copy.summary from CardStore.queue, and give it its own model site and budget, failing closed to today's fields. Separately, stop gold_headline cutting before prepositions: cut only at real clause punctuation, else keep the whole move under recommended and leave the subject to C1. Run one or two live calls first (Claude 5 thinking eats max_tokens).
items.blocked_on: To find the writer of the garbled headline (read-only, Rohit's permission): select card_id, builder_version, render_mode, capability_key, level, headline, recommended->>'what' as move, reject_code, reject_detail, created_at from cards where org_id=:org and (headline ilike '%calendar invite%' or headline ilike '%to body%'); then: select kind, cause, detail->'words' from card_events where card_id=:card order by occurred_at;
items.effect_on_cards: Subjects that are cut, stiff ('Needs a decision — …') or garbled, like 'Send calendar invites with meeting link to body'.
items.mistake: STEP-14 s14-D8 chose 'the move cut at a clause by code, no prompt change'. The cut pattern treats prepositions as clause starts, so a 60-character cut can drop the object and keep a dangling phrase.
items.correction: There are at least five headline writers, not four. The fifth is the P4 team/verify situation cards (builder team.emit.v1 = SITUATION_CARD_BUILDER, store.py:28). reason/team/emit._write_card writes their headline with clip(headline, HEADLINE_MAX=60) (emit.py:62, 81-83, 244), which hard-cuts at 59 characters and adds an ellipsis ('…'). Second detail: the 41-character body budget applies only to the 'Needs a decision — ' frame (60-19). For 'Unresolved — ' the budget is 47 (render.py:248-255).
items.verify_note: Confirmed: deliver/card_copy.py does not exist, and no 'cards.copy' or card_copy appears anywhere in genios_engine or migrations. _GOLD_CUT splits before to/with/for/on/in and similar words (card_builder.py:891-892). _gold_template is applied at card_builder.py:1142. HEADLINE_CAP=60 (render.py:26). state_not_command is at pipeline.py:1003, after review_copy for expert cards. The formula template 'Deliver {action} to {entity} today' is at general_v1.py:174. The executive_bridge headline is '{frame} — {goal}' or the bare goal (executive_bridge.py:103). The phrase 'calendar invites with meeting link' appears nowhere in .py/.md/.json/.yaml/.jsonl. Which writer produced it needs the production card row.

items.title: Question cards: brain and web Cards page are correct; the Mac app offers Done (422 not_offered, swallowed) and no Answer
items.expected: A question card offers Answer, Later and Don't-ask-me, never Done. A refused press says why and stays visible.
items.actual:
Brain: question cards offer answer, snooze and wrong (pipeline.py:316-320). Any other action returns 422 not_offered, and an answered card offers only snooze/requeue (actions.py:196-202).

Web: dashboard origin/main 2edfb86 has merged rohit/cards-ux, which has an Answer box and no Done on question cards.

Mac app (origin/main): DesktopAdvisor draws Done on every loop (line 492) and has no answer flow. act() removes the card optimistically and calls cardAction, whose request ends in .catch(() => {}). So the 422 is swallowed and the card returns on the next poll.
items.fix: Mac app: read render_mode and actions[] from the card (the readCard approach) and draw only offered buttons, adding an Answer box. Show refusals instead of swallowing them, undo the optimistic removal on failure, and send surface:'desktop'.
items.effect_on_cards: On the Mac, pressing Done on a question card does nothing and the card comes back, so the founder's answer is never given.
items.mistake: Desktop cardAction swallows every error by design (.catch(() => {})). A refusal nobody sees is a silent stop.
items.verify_note: Brain: QUESTION_ACTIONS=(answer, snooze, wrong) (pipeline.py:226, 316-320). QUESTION_OFFERS also admits requeue (actions.py:43). An answered card accepts only snooze/requeue (ANSWERED_OFFERS, actions.py:61, 196-200). Other actions return not_offered, which the route turns into 422 (routes.py:5631-5634). Mac app (dashboard origin/main): DesktopAdvisor act() removes the card optimistically (DesktopAdvisor.tsx:320-329). Done/Snooze/Not useful are drawn on every loop (lines 491-499). There is no answer flow. cardAction ends with .catch(() => {}) (api.ts:372-381). The app reads /cards (api.ts:303-304), so question cards reach it. Web: a question card shows Answer instead of Done (page.tsx:701-704) and has an answer textarea (page.tsx:850-863).

items.title: The Mac app's 'Not useful' sends 'wrong' with no reason; the brain refuses it (422 invalid_wrong_reason) and the app swallows it, so no verdict reaches L6
items.expected: Every 'wrong' carries one of the closed reasons the card offers (actions[].reasons / reason_groups), and a refusal is shown.
items.actual: Brain: ingest_action returns invalid_wrong_reason when reason is not in WRONG_REASONS, and the route turns that into 422. Mac: cardAction(loop.card_id, 'wrong') with reason '' sends reason: null, then .catch(() => {}). The web Feedback menu does send a reason.
items.fix: Mac app: open a reason picker from the card's reason_groups (four headings), with optional words, and send {action:'wrong', reason, words, scope, surface:'desktop'}. Surface the error. Do not default a reason server-side; the vocabulary rule says a verdict requires a closed reason.
items.blocked_on: To size it (read-only): select type, detail->>'surface' as surface, detail->>'reason' as reason, count(*) from human_events where org_id=:org and type like 'card.%' and occurred_at >= '2026-10-01' group by 1,2,3 order by 4 desc; a missing 'desktop' wrong means every Mac 'Not useful' was lost.
items.effect_on_cards: Pressing 'Not useful' on the Mac hides the card for a moment; it comes back, and calibration and corrections learn nothing.
items.verify_note: actions.py:102-104 returns invalid_wrong_reason when reason is not in WRONG_REASONS, and routes.py:5631-5634 maps it to 422. Mac 'Not useful' calls act(loop,'wrong') (DesktopAdvisor.tsx:497-499). cardAction then sends reason: reason || null and swallows the error (api.ts:372-381). The web FeedbackMenu sends a reason group (page.tsx:995, 1103) and shows the invalid_wrong_reason error (page.tsx:203).

items.title: C9 and version: the brain keeps each version's words and change, but the dashboard counts only card.rebuilt and ignores card.versioned and cards.version
items.expected: The panel says 'version N — what changed' (C9).
items.actual: Brain: file cards are versioned through card_lifecycle.version_card, which writes card.versioned with cause = the change, and version_of computes the changed fields and whether they are material. cards.version exists (0220) and GET /cards/{id} returns it via k.*. A formula refresh writes card.rebuilt with its words. Dashboard: versionOf counts only 'card.rebuilt' events, so an expert/L2 file card that was versioned shows the wrong version. 'What changed' is not shown.
items.fix: Dashboard: read card.version from the detail, and show the latest card.versioned cause and changed fields as 'what changed'. Brain: optionally serve the last change on GET /cards/{id}.
items.effect_on_cards: The version number is wrong on versioned file cards, and the panel cannot say what changed.
items.verify_note: card_lifecycle.py:147 VERSIONED='card.versioned' is written by version_card with cause=version.change (card_lifecycle.py:263-268). version_of computes change, changed and material (contracts/card_version.py:191-205). cards.version comes from migrations/0220_the_living_card.sql:31. card.rebuilt events carry words and version (store.py:575-581). Dashboard card-read.ts:595-598 counts only 'card.rebuilt', and page.tsx:785 uses that count. 'What changed' is never shown.

items.title: L4 auto-plans executions from every authoritative signal on each heartbeat; the DecisionObject is written to a table nothing reads; no human decides first
items.expected: L4's input is a DecisionObject that a human decides (approve, reject, defer, choose). Only an approved choice becomes an ExecutionObject carrying goal_refs and decision_request_id. Auto-planning from signals stops (human_decides per tenant).
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-008/00-ARCHITECTURE.md 'The layers' L4 row; 02-MIGRATION-PLAN.md §1 'L4 input … REPLACE' and §3.4 L4-1; GeniOS-009 STEP-G8 §2
items.actual: api/routes.py heartbeat calls run_executive for every org. plan_commitments turns each row of _PLANNABLE_SIGNALS into an execution with resolve_owner, with no human step. execution.v1 has goal: str and no goal id. None of these exist: executive/decisions.py, api/decision_routes.py, a decision_requests migration, a human_decides feature, context/checkin.py. L3's DecisionObject ({needed, who, what, by_when}) is written inside situation_interpretations.proposal, and that table is declared in UNREAD_WRITES ('nothing selects from it').
evidence: ls executive/decisions.py api/decision_routes.py context/checkin.py → No such file
items.fix: Build GeniOS-009 STEP-G8: migration decision_requests, contracts/decision.py, executive/decisions.py (open_requests_from_interpretations reading situation_interpretations, then decide, then to_execution), the human_decides feature in l4_activation, and the plan_commitments skip. Add GET/POST /v1/decisions and the record_result → reported_complete hook. Rohit switches human_decides on per tenant.
items.effect_on_cards: Commitments and reminders exist that no person chose. A decision card has no owner or decider and no link from Rohit's choice to the work.
items.verify_note: The heartbeat calls run_executive for each org in _executive_orgs, meaning every org with an active tenant_pack (routes.py:1517-1535, 1674-1687). No l4_activation feature gates it. plan_commitments goes from _PLANNABLE_SIGNALS through resolve_owner to build_execution and store.persist, with no human step (sweep.py:74-95, 173-238). run_executive is at sweep.py:483-493. execution.v1 has goal: str (contracts/execution.py:385). executive/decisions.py, api/decision_routes.py and context/checkin.py do not exist. No 'decision_request' or 'human_decides' appears in genios_engine or migrations. interpretation_of puts the decision {needed, who, what, by_when} in the interpretation (l2_admission.py:141-167, insert at 168-169). No code or script SELECTs from situation_interpretations, and it is listed in UNREAD_WRITES (table_coverage.py:133-140).

items.title: Calibration now runs (bug 1 fixed in shadow), but its would-mute and would-nudge results are read by nobody; the B22–B24 traps are still in the apply path
items.expected: Shadow calibration shows what it would do, so Rohit can decide whether to arm it (D13). Mutes are recorded, can be lifted, and never hide unrelated cards.
items.actual: The canonical_judgments CTE projects card_level (184269a0, in prod history), and run_calibration(apply=False) is the default. would_mute and would_nudge are stored only in calibration_runs.result. Readers are the idempotency check in calibrate.py:283 and a count(*) receipt. In the apply path, an applied mute or nudge still bumps tenant_packs.authority_revision, which hides every open card of the pack; a muted rule expires its signals' cards. No B22–B24 fix is present.
items.fix: Show the last shadow result (would_mute, would_nudge, with precision and n) on GET /feedback/precision or a learning screen. Do not arm calibration_apply until B22–B24 are fixed and Rohit answers D13.

items.correction: 'No B22–B24 fix is present' overstates it. B22, the part where a muted rule's cards vanish with no record, is addressed: the apply path expires them through card_lifecycle.expire_cards with cause RULE_MUTED, one card.expired event each (calibrate.py:415-430; card_lifecycle.py:65,109-121; added in 15a9bd70 on 2026-10-07). items.title: Why 'Antler Singapore admission' cannot become a goal automatically today
items.expected: A workstream the founder is actively pursuing, whose context is in the graph (Theresa, the Antler partner; the Singapore admission), is proposed as a goal for one-click approval and never becomes active on its own (Rohit's F2; source GOAL-01).
items.expected_source: F2 (Rohit); speedrun008/GeniOS-009/source/GeniOS-Goal-Achievement-Loop-Chat.md:10100-10104 (GOAL-01 'LLM infers a new departmental goal — does not become authoritative without approval')
items.actual: (1) The only automatic goal proposer is the brief drafter. It runs weekly, and only for orgs with at least one accepted brief line (reason/brief_review.py:24-25). A first draft happens only through the operator script scripts/draft_company_brief.py. It needs a real-LLM client (platform/wiring.py:290-297), and a failed draft loses the week (brief_review.py:58-60). (2) The drafter reads memory PATTERNS only: correspondents, domains, waves, introducers, meeting series, deadline domains, and at most the 40 most recent thread objectives in 180 days (reason/brief_patterns.py:37,44,108-113,257-262). It never reads context_situations, workstream files, expert_reviews or reasoning_results. (3) It is told to 'Propose only what is missing — never a line it already says' (brief_drafter.py:83-87), and store dedupe applies (platform/company_brief_store.py:99-118). An umbrella goal like 'Get into accelerator and incubator programs' therefore covers Antler, and the goals section is capped at 8 lines (brief_drafter.py:39). (4) The readers that do see the Antler file, R-7 expert and R-9 L2, cannot propose a goal. ExpertReview proposes only a kind (contracts/expert_review.py:256,279), which is written to section in_motion (reason/expert/kind_proposal.py:132-140). L2Judgment has no proposal field (contracts/reasoning_result.py:241-242). (5) No test expects it. tests/replays/specs/01-theresa… frames Theresa as an investor reconsideration whose business_subject is 'not Antler as an organization', with no goal obligation, and no golden founder case mentions Antler or Theresa.
items.fix: Short term, within the existing door: (a) run the drafter for tenants with no accepted line too (the first draft), and retry a failed week. (b) Add the open situations and workstream files with their kinds, plus the in-motion lines, to brief_patterns as pattern items, so the drafter can propose a goal per active workstream. The real fix is the L2 proposer (design item).
items.effect_on_cards: An active admission or fundraising thread never becomes a goal, so its cards stay 'Not linked to a goal', and nothing on the home page says the founder is pursuing it.
items.blocked_on: Production (read-only, Rohit's permission): select section,status,proposed_by,left(text,120),proposed_at,accepted_at from company_brief_lines where org_id=:org and section in ('goals','in_motion') order by proposed_at;  select week_key,outcome,proposed,finished_at from company_brief_reviews where org_id=:org order by week_key desc limit 10;  select field,left(value::text,160),occurred_at from graph_facts where org_id=:org and valid_to is null and value::text ilike '%antler%' order by occurred_at desc limit 20;  select file_id,status,reviewed_at from expert_reviews where org_id=:org and (file_id ilike '%antler%' or review::text ilike '%antler%') order by reviewed_at desc limit 10;  select subject_ref,status,lane,reasoned_at from reasoning_results where org_id=:org and (subject_ref ilike '%antler%' or result::text ilike '%antler%') order by reasoned_at desc limit 10;
items.mistake: The goal proposer was scoped to the STEP-07 drafter (patterns, weekly), which was designed to write a brief on day one, not to notice new workstreams.
items.correction: The mechanism holds: weekly review only for orgs with an accepted line (reason/brief_review.py:24-25); a failed draft loses the week (:58-60); the only other caller is scripts/draft_company_brief.py, and no API route calls the drafter; it needs a real-LLM client (platform/wiring.py:290-297). The drafter reads only source_events, graph_facts, graph_nodes and orgs (reason/brief_patterns.py:37,44,108-113,257-262). R-7 can propose only an in_motion kind (kind_proposal.py:132-140), and L2Judgment has no proposal field. Four details are wrong. (a) MAX_PER_SECTION=8 (brief_drafter.py:39) caps the goal proposals of ONE draft: the per-section counter in parse() (:156,:180) restarts each call. It does not cap the goals section of the brief. (b) Store dedupe (platform/company_brief_store.py:99-118) blocks only identical normalized text, or the same address or domain. A distinctly worded Antler goal would pass it. What blocks one is the prompt's 'Propose only what is missing' (brief_drafter.py:84) together with an umbrella goal, and the golden brief really holds 'Get into accelerator and incubator programs' (tests/replays/specs/founder/brief/company_brief.json:18-19). (c) Founder golden cases are forbidden by contract to use real names: tests/replays/founder_case.py:84-90 REAL_NAMES includes 'Theresa' and 'Antler'. So no founder case naming them is by design. The synthetic analogue F17 ('An accelerator moves the founder's application to interview') exists, and its authored answer ties it only in words to the umbrella goal ('Getting into accelerator programmes is one of the brief's goals'). (d) There is also replay spec tests/replays/specs/12-antler_exploratory_relationship_and_regional_aut.json (944b4f76). It models the Antler Singapore 2026 application from the program-operator side ([MODELLED]) and also has no goal field.

items.title: Plan gap: even after G1–G9, a workstream like Antler cannot become a goal of its own
items.expected: The plan contains a unit in which the L2 judgment infers a goal from a workstream it reads, L3 admits it as a proposal, and a human approves it (source GOAL-01; 06-CARDS-TARGET §4 'Proposed goal' card).
items.actual: STEP-G1 §2.1 mentions 'the drafter's, or later L2's' proposals, but no unit builds L2's. STEP-G1 §4 says 'The model only proposes, through the existing brief drafter', and 08-DECISIONS D7 names the drafter as the door. STEP-G2 §2.1 never prints proposed goals. STEP-G3 §3.1–§3.2 refuses GOAL_NOT_PRINTED ('Name only goals block G printed'), so L2 can only link Antler to an approved umbrella goal. The STEP-G3 §3.3 labels put the program cases F17, F19, F21, F22, F24 and F67 under 'Accelerator and incubator programs', so a single admission is a link, never its own goal. GeniOS-010 D-010-G2 wants monthly child goals through parent_goal_id, but no unit creates them. STEP-G4 §2 holds links to proposed goals. The 'Proposed goal' card in 06-CARDS-TARGET §4 has no build unit.
items.fix: Add units to the plan before building G1–G3: G1.6, a structured goal proposal from L3 admission (the door and its fields); G3.5, L2Judgment.proposed_goal with claim checks; G4.5, context/goal_admission.decide_goal_proposal; G6.8, the proposed-goal chip on the card and on the home page. Add a golden case F72, 'Antler Singapore application becomes a proposed goal', and mutation proofs for 'never active without a human'. Record Rohit's decision on granularity and the door (decision item).
items.effect_on_cards: Built exactly as written, the plan still leaves Rohit's main complaint ('Antler never became a goal') unfixed.
items.blocked_on: Rohit's decision goals-decision-goal-granularity-and-door
items.mistake: STEP-G1 waved at 'later L2's' proposals and D7 defaulted to the drafter, but no unit was written for L2. 06 promised a card kind that no step builds. G3's 'name only printed goals' rule was written without a companion rule for 'propose when none fits'.
items.verify_note: Every cited passage checks out. STEP-G1:44 ('the drafter's, or later L2's') has no unit, and STEP-G1 §4 (:186-189) says 'The model only proposes, through the existing brief drafter'. D7 names the drafter. STEP-G2:23,49,79 never print proposed goals. STEP-G3:76 defines GOAL_NOT_PRINTED, :92 says 'Name only goals block G printed', and :105 maps F17, F19, F21, F22, F24 and F67 to the umbrella goal. STEP-G4:44 holds a link to a proposed goal (goal_not_live). D-010-G2 (GeniOS-010/03-GOALS/README.md:92) needs parent_goal_id children, and no unit creates them. The plan also contradicts itself: 06-CARDS-TARGET.md:101's own example, 'make Join Gulf Launchpad a goal?', is a single-programme goal, the same shape as Antler, yet G3 labels every programme case under the umbrella. Caveat on the source: GOAL-01 (source/GeniOS-Goal-Achievement-Loop-Chat.md:8728) only says an LLM-inferred departmental goal must not become authoritative without approval. The LLM drafter meets its letter. The per-workstream L2 proposer comes from Rohit's F2 and the 06 §4 example, not from GOAL-01. Severity: this is a plan gap for unbuilt work and starves no card today, so P1 fits better than P0.

items.title: Missing design: L2 proposes a goal from a workstream, L3 admits it as a proposal, the founder approves in one click, and it reaches the card and the home page
items.expected: In GeniOS-008 terms: L2 (R-9 judgment) proposes, with evidence; L3 admits, holds or rejects in code; an inferred goal never becomes active without a human; L5 shows the proposal where the founder already looks, and one click approves it.
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-008/00-ARCHITECTURE.md 'The model rules' and 'Inside L3'; GeniOS-009/05-THE-SOURCE.md §5 invariants 2 and 7; F2
items.actual: Nothing exists. There is a precedent to copy: the R-7 expert's kind proposal (ExpertReview.proposed_kind → reason/expert/kind_proposal.propose_kind → company_brief_store.propose(proposed_by='expert_review', evidence=[review, file, cites])) at reason/expert/sweep.py:310-316. It shows that a per-file reader can already write a founder-decided proposal through the brief door.
evidence: genios_engine/api/company_brief_routes.py:127-150 (accept with no text already works: decide {decision:'accept'})
items.fix: CONTRACT (contracts/reasoning_result.py): L2Judgment.proposed_goal: GoalProposal | None. Fields: statement (≤200 chars, founder's words); why (≤300, claim-checked); evidence (printed ids, at least one, and at least one must show the company's own act: an outbound, an application or a meeting held); subject_ref and work_kind (filled by code from the request and the file, never by the model); parent_goal_ref (a goal: id block G printed, giving a child goal under the umbrella); metric (a METRICS key or null); target and deadline (only with a printed tool line or ev id in target_basis/deadline_basis); owner (a person printed in the file; code resolves the seat). Refusals: GOAL_PROPOSAL_NO_EVIDENCE, UNPRINTED_REF, TARGET_NOT_PRINTED, DEADLINE_NOT_PRINTED, PARENT_NOT_PRINTED. A failing proposal is dropped and the run kept. Prompt line: 'If this file is work the company is pursuing (an application, a raise, a certification, a hire) and no goal in block G names it at that level, propose one, citing the lines; never for a monitor or suppress subject.' Block G lists pending proposals separately, for dedupe. Cost: same R-9 call, about 60–120 more output tokens, 0 calls when nothing moved. L3 (new context/goal_admission.py, pure decide plus a write inside the L2 sweep's admission savepoint, reason/l2/sweep.py:421-429): REJECT when the subject's admission is REJECT, or the lane is suppress or monitor. HOLD (reason recorded) when the situation's admission is HOLD, the proposal duplicates a live goal or a pending proposal (same subject_ref or normalized statement), the founder rejected a match within REJECTED_QUIET_DAYS=90, the org's weekly cap (e.g. 3 new proposals) is reached, or no evidence shows the company's own act. ADMIT writes a PROPOSAL only: company_goals with status='proposed', source='inferred', evidence_refs, subject_ref, result_fingerprint and the proposed fields (or a brief goals line with a proposal jsonb, per the decision). Never active; the DB check company_goals_live_is_approved_ck enforces it. ONE CLICK: POST /v1/goals/{id}/approve {revision}, with no text, sets approved_by and approved_at, status active, and copies the proposed metric, deadline, owner and parent; 'Edit' is optional; 'Not a goal' rejects (quiet for 90 days). The Goals page pre-fills the four answers from the proposal and shows its evidence quotes. A 'Make this a goal?' chip appears on the Antler card's Goal row (cards/page.tsx:925), and home §1 shows 'N goals waiting for you' with the same button. AFTER APPROVAL: the next sweep's l3.goals_sync makes it active; G2's goal_set moves the Antler file's fingerprint, so it is re-judged once; G3 writes advances goal:<id>; G4 links it on ADMIT; G6 renders 'Moves: Get admitted to Antler Singapore — advances · <printed date>' on the card; GET /v1/goals serves it to the Goals page, and to home §1 when the deadline falls this month (D-010-G2). TESTS: golden F72 (an Antler application thread, the partner's reply, no matching goal → proposal → admitted as proposed → approve → link and goal line); mutation proofs: an active status without approved_by is refused; skipping dedupe re-proposes on the second sweep; dropping the own-act evidence rule lets a newsletter propose a goal. Wire it on the L2 path explicitly (see the kind-proposal item); optionally mirror it on R-7 ExpertReview the way proposed_kind is, for tenants still on the expert path.
items.effect_on_cards: With this in place, the Antler card says it moves a goal, the Goals page shows the goal, and home §1 counts it, after one click from the founder.
items.blocked_on: Rohit: the decision item (granularity, door, weekly cap)
items.verify_note: No L2 or L3 goal proposal exists. The only writers of brief proposals are reason/brief_drafter.py:248 and reason/expert/kind_proposal.py:132 (called from reason/expert/sweep.py:310-316). context/founder_corrections.py:177 writes only accepted 'preferences' lines. kind_proposal.py ends at :151, not 155. The precedent holds: proposed_by='expert_review' with evidence [{review, file, cites}]. A one-click accept already works: CompanyBriefDecision.text is optional (api/company_brief_routes.py:57-62), and store.accept keeps the proposal's words when words is None (company_brief_store.py:185).

items.title: On the L2 card path, the model is asked for proposed_kind but nothing writes it, so kind proposals stop when l2_cards is on
items.expected: With l2_cards on, an admitted L2 judgment 'decides it exactly as an expert review does' (platform/l4_activation.py:118-121), including the founder-facing kind proposal that the R-7 path writes.
items.actual: The L2 prompt schema is expert.SCHEMA merged with L2_SCHEMA (reason/l2/prompt.py:126), so it asks for proposed_kind (reason/expert/prompt.py:203). reason/l2/sweep.py never calls propose_kind; only reason/expert/sweep.py:310-316 does. With l2_cards on, the R-7 call is not made (l4_activation.py:118-121), so the expert's kind proposals and corrections (F53, F132, F157) silently stop. No test under tests/reason/l2 covers it.
items.fix: In reason/l2/sweep.py, for each admitted file result with result.review.proposed_kind and checked.stands('kind'), call kind_proposal.propose_kind inside the write step. Add a PG test on the L2 path plus a mutation proof. The goal proposer must be wired the same way.
items.effect_on_cards: After G0.2 switches l2_cards on, a fund misfiled as sales or a programme behaving like its fund is never offered for correction, so its cards read the wrong playbook.
items.mistake: L2 rebuild C1 (de795bb8) reused the review row and the card path but not the proposal side effect of the expert pass.
items.verify_note: reason/l2/prompt.py:126 merges expert.SCHEMA, which includes proposed_kind (reason/expert/prompt.py:203). The parsed ExpertReview carries it, and reason/expert/verify.py:1140 checks it. But reason/l2/sweep.py (_file_review :120-138, _write_file_review :141-157) never calls propose_kind; grep finds it only in reason/expert. With l2_cards on, the expert sweep sets l2_judges (reason/expert/sweep.py:171) and returns at :277-285, before any R-7 call or propose_kind. No test under tests/reason/l2 references proposed_kind or propose_kind.

SAMPLE_GOALS : []', and :686-687 renders MonthOnly, which draws greyed SAMPLE_GOALS as a placeholder (:388-395). homepage/live.ts:290-298 hard-codes 'Goals formed' as '0' with 'Goals are coming next', and :374 always pushes 'No goals set yet…'. goals/live.ts:201 liveGoalsView maps the accepted brief 'goals' lines into goal cards, so the two surfaces disagree.

items.title: Goals page: approval needs typing to be useful, the answers become free text, and the drafter's evidence is never shown
items.expected: A proposed goal shows where GeniOS saw it (its proof) and is approved in one click, with target, deadline and owner pre-filled as structured fields.
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-010/03-GOALS/01-GOALS-PAGE.md §1.4, §5 ('After G1 they should land as structured fields (PATCH /v1/goals/{id})'); F2
items.actual: goals-page.tsx:347-396 renders four free-text inputs. finalGoalLine (goals/live.ts:185) joins the answers into the line's text, which decideGoalProposal then sends as the accepted words. Target, deadline and owner therefore end up inside the statement, and G1's sync (STEP-G1 §3 G1.3, words only) would carry them as text with no deadline field. Approve is enabled with zero answers (disabled only for sample/busy), so one click works but yields a goal with no target, deadline or owner. Proof: proofOf (goals/live.ts:74) reads statement/field/question/inference/because/text, but drafter evidence items carry pattern/kind/address/name/about/title/domain/last (reason/brief_drafter.py:200-205; reason/brief_patterns.py:241-262), so every proposal falls back to the generic 'GeniOS proposed it from what it read' (goals/live.ts:179).
items.fix: Render pattern evidence (about, title, address/domain, last date) in proofOf. Once proposals carry structured fields (design item), pre-fill the four answers and send them as fields (PATCH /v1/goals or the approve body), never concatenated into the statement.
items.effect_on_cards: The founder cannot see why GeniOS proposed a goal, and an approved goal has no deadline or target that code can use.
items.verify_note: goals-page.tsx:363-374 renders four free-text inputs (maxLength 60). The Approve button (:390-396) is disabled only on sample or busy, and it sends finalGoalLine (goals/live.ts:185-193), which folds target, deadline, owner and done-when into the text. That text is cut at 200 characters, the same as MAX_LINE_CHARS (contracts/company_brief.py:63), so long answers are silently truncated. proofOf (live.ts:74-84) reads statement, field, question, inference, because and text. Drafter evidence is {pattern, kind, …pattern fields} (brief_drafter.py:200-205), and every pattern item (brief_patterns.py:164-166, 241-262) lacks all six keys. So every proposal falls back to the generic text at live.ts:179.

items.title: Decision needed: may L2 propose goals, at what granularity, and through which door
items.expected: One recorded answer before G1 is built, because it changes G1's schema and the G3 prompt.
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-009/08-DECISIONS.md D2, D7 (defaults only); GeniOS-010/03-GOALS/README.md D-010-G2
items.actual: D7 defaults to 'yes, as proposed', but names only the drafter. Nothing decides: (a) whether the R-9 L2 judgment may propose goals; (b) granularity: an umbrella goal ('Get into accelerator programs') with child goals per workstream ('Antler Singapore admission') through parent_goal_id, or links only; (c) the door: keep the brief as the only door and add a proposal jsonb to company_brief_lines, or let L3 write company_goals(status='proposed') directly with POST /v1/goals/{id}/approve; (d) a weekly cap on new proposals.
items.fix: Rohit answers D9 (L2 may propose: yes or no), D10 (child goals under umbrella goals: yes or no), D11 (door: brief plus proposal jsonb, or company_goals direct), and D12 (cap, default 3 a week). Recommended defaults: yes; yes; company_goals direct with the brief kept in sync; 3 a week.
items.blocked_on: Rohit
items.verify_note: 08-DECISIONS D7's default names only the drafter, and STEP-G1 §2.1 says 'The brief stays the door'. D-010-G2 assumes parent_goal_id children. No recorded answer covers (a)–(c). On (d): the drafter path already has a de facto cap, at most 8 goal proposals per weekly draft (brief_drafter.py:39,180), plus store dedupe and the rejected-line quiet window (company_brief_store.py:107-117). items.title: Delegate is drawn on every card but cannot be pressed: the brain has no delegate route (C5)
items.expected: Done · Delegate (a team member, or an agent) · Later · Feedback. Hand-over sets the card's assignee and records a card event; an agent hand-over creates a delegation proposal the founder approves.
items.actual: Web Cards has DELEGATE_LIVE = false: 'Hand over' and 'Ask it' are disabled with a lock. The brain's card action set has no delegate verb, and no /cards/{id}/delegate route exists. Mac 0.3.4 shows Delegate with people: [] (no team members at all) and no press.
items.fix: Build C5: POST /cards/{card_id}/delegate {to_seat} (owner/admin; set cards.assignee, a human.card_action event with cause delegate). Then set DELEGATE_LIVE=true on the web and give the Mac app the same press and the members list. Keep 'to an agent' locked while Agents stays locked (Rohit's call).
items.effect_on_cards: A card that belongs to a teammate cannot be routed from the card, so it stays in the founder's queue.
items.correction: The web lock, the missing verb and the missing /cards/{id}/delegate route all hold. But the claim that 'the brain has no delegate route' is too broad. The agent half of hand-over already exists: POST /v1/delegations takes {card_id, play, params, agent_id} (delegation_routes.py:85-100), and executive/delegation.create_proposal accepts card_id (executive/delegation.py:402-421). It comes with /v1/delegations/{id}/approve and /reject (:124, :135), and main.py:217-218 registers it. The dashboard already has a client, src/lib/api-delegations.ts (used by components/governance/agent-actions.tsx), but the Cards page does not call it. What is truly missing is the hand-over to a person (set cards.assignee plus a card event) and a server-built play from the card, which is the C5 spec in 06-CARDS/01-INTEGRATION.md §C5. POST /v1/executive/commitments/{execution_id}/reassign (executive_routes.py:331) reassigns commitments, not cards.
items.verify_note: Confirmed parts: cards/page.tsx:79-85 has DELEGATE_LIVE=false, and :1232 and :1253 render 'Hand over' and 'Ask it' disabled with a Lock icon. actions.py:36 BUTTONS = {run_play, do_it_myself, snooze, wrong, requeue, answer}. The card routes are only GET /cards/{id}, POST /cards/{id}/action and GET /cards/{id}/timeline. Mac desktop-ux MenuApp.tsx:380 has people: [].

items.title: The Mac app on main (0.2.4) and the downloadable 0.2.0 lose presses: 'Not useful' and Done on question cards are refused and swallowed
items.expected: Only the buttons a card offers are pressable, and a refusal is said, never swallowed (M1–M5 in 06-CARDS/03). surface='desktop' is sent so History can say where you acted.
items.actual: cardAction POSTs {action, reason: reason||null} with no surface and ends in .catch(() => {}). 'Not useful' sends wrong with reason null, and the brain answers 422 invalid_wrong_reason. Done shows on every card, including question cards, which the brain refuses with not_offered. The card is removed optimistically and comes back on refresh. There is no Answer button. Expert why rows render ': undefined'. Who the card is about is guessed from the headline by regex.
evidence: dashboard origin/main:Extension/src/desktop/DesktopAdvisor.tsx:321-329 (optimistic remove), 492-499 (Done/Snooze/Not useful on every card), 129-135 (whyLine), 156 (entityOf)
items.fix: Ship rohit/desktop-ux (pressCard with surface='desktop', refusals said, the web reader, Answer on question cards), which fixes M1–M5. See surfaces-mac-three-versions.
items.effect_on_cards: For anyone on 0.2.x, 'Not useful' feedback never reaches L6, question cards cannot be answered from the desktop, and dismissed cards reappear, which reads as 'weird'.
items.mistake: The fix exists (rohit/desktop-ux) but was never merged or released.
items.correction: The behaviour holds, but the brain citations are off. The not_offered refusal for question cards is at deliver/actions.py:201-202 (QUESTION_OFFERS is at :43). For answered cards it is at :199-200. Lines 92-93 are only the ingest_action signature. invalid_wrong_reason is at actions.py:102-104, and routes.py:5626-5628 turns it into an HTTP 422.
items.verify_note: Checked on dashboard main. Extension/src/desktop/api.ts:372-381: cardAction sends {action, reason: reason||null} with no surface and ends in .catch(() => {}). DesktopAdvisor.tsx:320-327: act() removes the card from the list before the call returns (optimistic) and calls cardAction with no reason. :491-500: Done, Snooze and 'Not useful' sit on every card, and there is no Answer button. :129-134: whyLine prints `${fieldLabel('')}: ${value}` for any row that is not expertise. The expert's situation row {sentence, inference, source:'expert_check'} (deliver/pipeline.py:293) has no field and no statement, so it renders ': undefined'. :156 entityOf(headline) guesses who the card is about with a regex. tauri.conf.json is 0.2.4. The downloadable zip's Info.plist says 0.2.0, and that build's cardAction (9f83fc7:Extension/src/desktop/api.ts:314-323) is the same.

items.title: The Screen page and the desktop's screen items depend on migration 0250 being applied in production
items.expected: 0250 is applied at boot (apply_migrations), so GET /v1/followups can select read_by and due_phrase.
items.actual: followups.listing now selects read_by, due_phrase and graph_written_at. If the database booted read-only ('DEGRADED BOOT') and 0250 did not land, every /v1/followups read fails. Whether it is applied in production is unknown.
evidence: genios_engine/main.py:89-96 (boot apply; read-only path logs DEGRADED BOOT)
items.fix: Harsh runs the read-only check below. If 0250 is missing, apply it (or restart the brain with a writable DB so boot applies it).
items.blocked_on: select filename from schema_migrations where filename like '0250%'; select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_name='screen_followups' and column_name in ('read_by','due_phrase');
items.effect_on_cards: None on cards. If missing, Screen shows no items and the Mac Pending list loses screen items.
items.correction: The dependency is wider than GET /v1/followups. The shared column list _COLS (reason/moments/followups.py:318-319) names read_by, due_phrase and graph_written_at, and every screen_followups path uses it. That covers the device slice open_items (:397), the capture upsert's RETURNING (:654, which also writes read_by and due_phrase), resolve (:712, :715), snooze (:735, :738), get_item (:750) and listing (:781). The moment routes pass read_by and due_phrase to F.upsert (moment_routes.py:515, :610). Without 0250, screen capture writes, the desktop's open-item slice, resolve/snooze and the Screen page would all fail. Not only the Screen read would break. graph_written_at itself comes from 0162, so it is not at risk.
items.verify_note: Boot runs apply_migrations and crashes on failure. The only path that keeps serving silently is ReadOnlyDatabaseError, which logs 'DEGRADED BOOT' (main.py:86-96). A missing 0250 would therefore show either as a crash loop or as a DEGRADED BOOT log line. Only production can answer whether it was applied. Read-only SQL for Rohit/Harsh: select filename from schema_migrations where filename like '0250%'; select column_name from information_schema.columns where table_name='screen_followups' and column_name in ('read_by','due_phrase');

items.title: Goals and Screen read cards with their own mapper: 'What to do' shows a verdict code, and inference labels show as proof
items.expected: One reader for a card everywhere (lib/card-read.ts readCard/ownCard). The move is shown in words, quotes are shown, and inference labels never appear as proof.
items.actual: goals/live.ts cardItem sets recommended = decision.recommendation.verdict. The brain's projection fills that with codes such as 'review_source', 'reply' or a play id. proofOf prints row.inference ('an inference, not a quote') as evidence and drops quotes. Screen imports the same cardItem for the cards an item fed, so one card reads differently on Cards, Goals and Screen.
evidence: speedrun008/GeniOS-010/06-CARDS/03-WHAT-WAS-THERE.md G1 (the stand-in brain hid it by putting a sentence there)
items.fix: Map Goals' and Screen's cards through readCard/ownCard and render the existing CardItem from a CardRead. Delete proofOf and the verdict read.
items.effect_on_cards: On Goals and Screen, a card's 'what to do' reads as a code ('reply'), and its proof is a label, not a quote.
items.mistake: Goals was built with its own mapper before Cards built readCard. The stand-in brain (02-DASHBOARD-HOME/tools/mock_brain.py) put a sentence where the real brain sends a code, so the render checks passed.
items.verify_note: goals/live.ts:94 sets recommended = str(rec.verdict). routes.py:5120-5137 fills verdict with codes: 'review_source', card.get('play') or reason_code, 'reply', 'deliver', 'follow_up'. proofOf (goals/live.ts:74-84) prefers statement, field/value, question, inference, because, text. It never reads quotes, and it prints row.inference, which the brain fills with the SITUATION_IS label 'the expert's reading of the file — an inference, not a quote' (decide.py:337; why row at pipeline.py:293). screen/live.ts:19 imports cardItem, and :193 uses it. 06-CARDS/03-WHAT-WAS-THERE.md G1 and G2 list both as Open. One more defect in the same mapper: cardItem maps every entry of decision.confidence (goals/live.ts:100-104), and level() returns 'medium' for anything that is not a number (:67-70). The brain's block (routes.py:5086-5100) has null dimensions, a list 'absent' and a string 'source'. So an absent dimension, plus 'Absent' and 'Source' chips, are all drawn as 'medium' confidence on Goals and Screen (intel/parts.tsx:262-275).

items.title: Cards read thin, repeated or garbled on every surface: the card writer (C1), the expert's result (C2) and per-card context (C6) are unbuilt
items.expected: Each card has its own clear subject, two lines (what to do and how), steps, the result of doing it, and context tied to its own thread. 'Every card's details and scenario must be its own.'
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-010/06-CARDS/01-INTEGRATION.md §5 C6, C2, C1; 06-CARDS/02-CARD-DEFINITION.md; memory cards-ux-analysis-22-oct round 3
items.actual: No deliver/card_copy.py and no cards.copy column. The gold block has no act/done_when, so 'what doing it gets you' is stock or empty. _meeting_neighbors and _commitment_neighbors attach the subject node's last 4 meetings and 3 promises to every card on that node. The surfaces then hide every text another open card repeats (sharedTexts/sharedLines) and count it as 'N lines read the same', so cards come out thin. Garbled headlines ('Send calendar invites with meeting link to body') and repeated one-liners ('70 days since they wrote') come from the brain's writer.
evidence: grep genios_engine and migrations: no card_copy, cards.copy, goal_refs
memory desktop-accessibility-and-adhoc-builds.md ('card one-liners repeating'); cards-ux-analysis-22-oct.md ('Open: garbled headlines')
items.fix: In order: C6 (keep only meetings and commitments on this card's thread or evidence), then C2 (gold.act and done_when as checked words → card result and success_signal), then C1 (deliver/card_copy.py, one claim-checked model call per new card version, its own budget, migration for cards.copy). Before any paid pass, test one or two live calls with max_tokens sized for thinking.
depends_on: Rohit's OK for a read-only production query to confirm cards anchor on one node (C6)
items.blocked_on: select subject_node_id, count(*) from cards c join signals s on s.signal_id=c.signal_id where c.org_id='<rohit org>' and c.state in ('queued','surfaced','snoozed','delivered') group by 1 order by 2 desc limit 10;
items.effect_on_cards: Fewer distinct lines per card, identical details across cards, no 'what doing it gets you', and unclear headlines. This is the 'weird' cards complaint (F2).
items.correction: C1 and C6 hold, but the C2 detail is overstated. done_when does reach the card. reason/expert/decide.py:278-291 puts the checked done_when into the play's success_events (_done at :266-271 falls back to '<headline> — done' when the check withholds it). deliver/pipeline.py:90 carries those as play_success_events, and card_builder._play_success (:233-236) writes them to success_signal. What never reaches the card is the expert's scenarios.act ('if you act now'). It exists in contracts/expert_review.py (Scenarios, :228; serialised at :374) but nothing reads it into the card. So 'what doing it gets you' is the checked done_when, or the stock '<move> — done', never the expert's result. The gold block at decide.py:323-330 does lack act and done_when, as stated.
items.verify_note: Confirmed: there is no deliver/card_copy.py (ls genios_engine/deliver), and grep finds no card_copy, cards.copy or goal_refs. _commitment_neighbors (routes.py:5225-5249) and _meeting_neighbors (:5252-5272) select by the subject node only and return out[:3] and out[:4]. Dashboard card-read.ts:513-527 (sharedTexts), :530-568 (ownCard) and :580-592 (sharedLines) hide repeated text and count leftOut. The garbled and repeated one-liners are a memory claim only (cards-ux-analysis-22-oct.md:99; desktop-accessibility-and-adhoc-builds.md:17), not measured on production cards.

items.title: Cards past the 40th never load their detail, even when opened
items.expected: Every open card can be opened and acted on. The queue carries what the list draws, and details load only for the opened card (C3).
items.actual: loadDetails fetches /cards/{id} for the first MAX_DETAILS=40 open cards only, and opening a card does not force its detail. For card 41 and on, the row's tool tags stay a pulsing skeleton, the panel says 'Reading the card…' forever, and the buttons fall back to defaults. The Goals page has the same 40 cap. The brain queue still lacks output_lane, business_subject, by_when and context_tags (C3 unbuilt).
items.fix: Dashboard: when a card is opened and its detail is missing, call loadDetails with that card forced. Brain: C3 (queue adds output_lane, business_subject, relationship_role, by_when, version, context_tags, from_screen) so the list needs no per-card fetch.
items.effect_on_cards: Only bites when more than 40 cards are open. Those cards cannot be read or properly acted on.
items.verify_note: cards/page.tsx:78 MAX_DETAILS=40. At :239-243, loadDetails slices to 40 BEFORE applying force, so even the forced reload after a press (:381) never loads card 41 or later. openCard (:417) only sets selected, and :312 loads the timeline, not the detail. For those cards the row shows a pulsing skeleton for tool tags (:669) and the panel shows 'Reading the card…' (:839). readCard's offers fall back to defaults when there are no actions (card-read.ts:439-441). goals-page.tsx:443 and :469 apply the same cap. Brain CardStore.queue (store.py:772-786, all three doors) selects no output_lane, business_subject, by_when or context_tags, and GET /cards (routes.py:5454) returns queue() as it is.

items.title: Web Cards offers Feedback on answered question cards, which the brain refuses, and the error text says 'give feedback'
items.expected: Only what the server offers on a card is pressable ('never a button it refuses').
items.actual: The Feedback MenuButton is drawn on every open card. It uses LEGACY_WRONG when the card's actions carry no 'wrong'. An answered question card offers only snooze (ANSWERED_OFFERS = snooze, requeue), so Feedback gets 422 not_offered. The page then says 'This card does not take that. Answer it, put it off, or give feedback.' Mac 0.3.4 locks Feedback in the same state, so the two surfaces disagree.
items.fix: Draw Feedback only when the card's actions include 'wrong'. Make the not_offered sentence list read.offers rather than fixed advice.
items.effect_on_cards: A press that is refused, with advice to repeat it.
items.correction: The behaviour holds, but the brain refusal is at deliver/actions.py:197-200 (an answered question card refuses any action not in ANSWERED_OFFERS), not at :90-91, which is snooze_until. ANSWERED_ACTIONS (:59) offers only snooze and is written onto the card at :354. ANSWERED_OFFERS = {snooze, requeue} is at :61.
items.verify_note: cards/page.tsx:1020 draws the Feedback MenuButton with no offers check. card-read.ts:425 falls back to LEGACY_WRONG (:141-146: not_relevant, wrong_facts, bad_timing) when the actions carry no 'wrong'. A valid reason passes the reason check (actions.py:102) and then hits not_offered, which the API returns as 422 (routes.py:5626-5628). friendlyError (cards/page.tsx:197-198) then says 'This card does not take that. Answer it, put it off, or give feedback.' Mac desktop-ux MenuApp.tsx:410-419 sets feedback to null with feedbackLockedWhy on answered cards, so the two surfaces disagree.

items.title: Resources: manual entries vanish on reload, edit and delete hit routes that do not exist, and settings are local-only
items.expected: Manual context can be listed, edited and deleted through brain routes. Controls change brain behaviour or are not shown.
items.expected_source: GeniOS-010 ground rule 1 (00-START-HERE); dashboard origin/main:src/lib/api.ts doc comments
items.actual: The brain has only POST /api/org/{org}/manual-context. listManualContext (GET) is imported but never called, so entries live in local state, seeded from an empty mock, and disappear on reload. deleteManualContext (DELETE …/{id}) and updateManualContext (PATCH …/{id}) have no brain route, and their errors are swallowed with catch {}. 'Extraction Preferences' toggles write only localStorage. 'File Type Authority Weights' is a hard-coded list.
items.fix: Either add GET/PATCH/DELETE manual-context routes in the brain, or remove list/edit/delete and say 'saved to memory' after POST. Remove or wire the local-only toggles and the fixed weights table.
items.effect_on_cards: Manual context the founder adds still reaches the brain via POST. The page misreports it.
items.verify_note: The brain route list has only POST /api/org/{org_id}/manual-context (workspace_routes.py:335): no GET, PATCH or DELETE. Dashboard api.ts:1633-1643 (list, delete) and :1852-1861 (PATCH update) exist. resources-page.tsx imports listManualContext (:31) but never calls it. Entries start from mockManualEntries = [] (:103, :166). handleDeleteEntry swallows errors with catch {} (:285-290), and the edit handler does too (:1384-1389). 'Extraction Preferences' (:1751) reads and writes localStorage 'genios_resource_prefs' (:1732, :1742). 'File Type Authority Weights' (:1797-1810) is a hard-coded list.

items.expected: 'Situations formed' = situations newly formed this week; 'Situations closed' = situations resolved this week with an outcome checked.
items.actual: situations_7d counts active context_situations with computed_at in 7 days, which includes every recompute, not just new ones. items.fix: Count situations by first-seen time (created_at) and resolved situations by resolved_at. Drop the fixed fields from home-summary. In the GeniOS-008 target, read L3-admitted situations.

The main writer's upsert sets computed_at = excluded.computed_at on every recompute (context/situations.py:1259) and leaves first_seen_at alone, so 'formed' counts recomputes. first_seen_at would be the true formation time. 'Situations closed · outcome checked' reuses the 'verified' card (homepage live.ts:304-313), which is outcomes_7d = execution_outcomes rows (home_routes.py:227-228, :317). The brain still ships coverageChange 0 (:298), intervention delta '+0%' and [max(4, intervention)]*12 bars (:322-323). git grep finds no dashboard src/product reader of coverageChange or the intervention card.

items.expected: A card is what · why · now · evidence · unknowns · options · authority · actions · receipt. Five lanes, including suppress with a why-not receipt. A six-dimension confidence vector.
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-008/00-ARCHITECTURE.md 'Cards — five lanes, a confidence vector'
items.actual: The web groups four lanes (decision, conflict, question, waiting) and shows urgency only (06-CARDS/03 C10 Open). card_builder emits the old C/U/I/R scalars. No dashboard file reads confidence_vector, unknowns or why-not. /v1/executive/why-not exists with no surface caller. Quotes carry no sender or date (C4), and there is no 'this is right' verdict (C7).
evidence: grep 'why-not|confidence_vector|unknowns' in dashboard origin/main src and Extension/src: no hits
items.fix: After L2's ReasoningResult carries the six dimensions (L2-9), add them to card.v1 and render them as named dots. Add a 'held back, and why' view off /v1/executive/why-not. Build C4 (quote sender and date) and C7 (a 'right' action).
items.effect_on_cards: The founder cannot see how sure GeniOS is, what is unknown, or what was held back.
items.correction: 'Shows urgency only' holds for the Cards page (06-CARDS/03 C10). The Goals and Screen pages, however, draw a 'Confidence' block (intel/parts.tsx:262-275, fed by goals/live.ts:90-104). That block is not the architecture's six-dimension vector, and its nulls render as 'medium'.

GET /v1/executive/why-not exists (executive_routes.py:76), and git grep finds no 'why-not', 'why_not' or 'confidence_vector' anywhere in dashboard main src/Extension/src or desktop-ux. decide.py:357 carries quotes as a bare list. actions.py:36 has no 'right'.

items.title: Nothing stops a push or merge to the production branch while CI is red
items.expected: Code reaches production only from a SHA whose CI is green: CI 'is the safety net every refactor stands on', and the guards 'run in CI' and turn it red.
items.expected_source: .github/workflows/ci.yml:1 header; speedrun008/GeniOS-008/01-RULES.md Rule 3; speedrun008/YC-II W27/STEP-17-TO-BUILD-real-tests.md §3.4 ('a failure blocks the next')
items.actual: There is no branch protection on any branch, and no required status checks. From 6 Sep (05f73d84) to 21 Oct (21b7ae10) the production branch had 61 CI runs, all red. The last green before that was c1dd89b3 on 2 Sep, and the next green was 0cc8d83c on 22 Oct. The 18 Oct merge c501eec9 (823 commits) never had a CI run of its own: harsh/mvp has no run between 84f00a40 (11 Oct) and 21b7ae10 (21 Oct). The first run that contained it, on 21 Oct, was red in golden-pg and database. The causes were cassette misses F03 F07 F14 F24 F55 F56; F13/F29 re-decided on an unchanged sweep (bisected to L3 2b ae5b5c7a); and a re-read ladder statement timeout. All three came from code that had already been merged for production, and all three were fixed only on 22 Oct (G0.1).
evidence: GitHub API actions/runs?branch=harsh/mvp (247 runs): window 2026-09-02T08:00..2026-10-22T14:00 = 61 runs, 61 failure; last success c1dd89b3 2026-09-02; next success 0cc8d83c 2026-10-22

Run 39633828127 (21b7ae10): golden-pg failure (check-run 119338845374 annotations: CassetteMiss at the expert and r1 sites), database failure (check-run 119338845521: test_the_compiled_lane_skips_an_unchanged_subject F13/F29, test_the_gate_is_counted, test_the_ladder_never_starves_pg QueryCanceled)

git log --first-parent origin/harsh/mvp: c501eec9 2026-10-18 → 21b7ae10 2026-10-21 with no CI run between (actions/runs created=2026-10-12..2026-10-23, non-therohitji actors: only 21b7ae10 and 0cc8d83c)
speedrun008/GeniOS-009/03-LOG.md:15 (G0.1: three causes, all from Harsh's rebuild; fixes 3d5a6a3d, 8d1de446, 269400dc)
git show 8d1de446: 'F13/F29 re-decided … exposed by L3 2b (ae5b5c7a, bisected)'
items.effect_on_cards: From 20 Oct until the 22 Oct fixes were deployed, the production branch carried code that re-decided unchanged subjects (extra model spend and card churn) and a 24.5 s re-read query (40,804 correlated subqueries), and CI flagged it only after the merge. Any future red merge will reach Rohit's cards the same way.
items.mistake: The prod branch was merged and pushed while red for 46 days. c501eec9 was pushed together with the 19–21 Oct rebuild commits in one push, so the 823-commit merge result was never tested before production received it. STEP-17 §3.4 wrote the gate as a runbook step (08-FOR-HARSH §0.2), not as a branch rule.
items.fix: In GitHub settings, protect harsh/mvp (and speedrun008). Require the status checks test, database and golden-pg, require the branch to be up to date, and forbid force pushes. Harsh merges speedrun008 only at a SHA whose run is green, through a PR into harsh/mvp.
items.blocked_on: Repository admin rights on themoronss/genios-brain (Rohit or Harsh) to enable branch protection.
items.verify_note: Measured via the public GitHub API. /branches for harsh%2Fmvp, speedrun008 and main all return protected=false and required_status_checks.enforcement_level=off. /rules/branches/harsh%2Fmvp and /rulesets are both [], so no ruleset exists either. The 247 harsh/mvp runs are all by hars123h. In the window 2026-09-02T08:00..2026-10-22T14:00 there are 61 runs and all 61 failed. The last success is c1dd89b3 (2026-09-02T07:54Z), the first failure after it is 05f73d84 (2026-09-06), and the next success is 0cc8d83c (2026-10-22T14:29Z). In run 39633828127 (21b7ae10), golden-pg failed on CassetteMiss: F03/F07/F14/F24 at the expert site, F55/F56 at r1. The database job failed on F13/F29 're-decided on an unchanged sweep', test_the_gate_is_counted, and the ladder test's QueryCanceled; the annotations match. 8d1de446 gives the cause as 'exposed by L3 2b (ae5b5c7a, bisected)'. The merge itself is 824 commits including c501eec9 (823 plus the merge). New detail: the GitHub push events show a single push 84f00a40→21b7ae10 at 2026-10-21T16:19:50Z, carrying 869 commits. That push included 75d08481, b9a21d91, 351de120, c501eec9 and all of Harsh's 19–21 Oct work. So nothing reached origin/harsh/mvp between 11 and 21 Oct. c501eec9 could not have had its own run, and its CI result arrived about 1.5 h after it was already on the production branch. Also, every harsh/mvp head carries a failing 'Vercel' commit status (0cc8d83c and 21b7ae10: state failure). A required-checks rule would have to account for that.

GET /health/readiness (genios_engine/api/routes.py:156-201) runs platform/receipts.evaluate per tenant. Its own docstring calls that 'the same list the release-gate CLI runs', i.e. scripts/runtime_receipts.py. (2) The dashboard admin has three tabs: growth, accounts and money (src/app/dashboard/admin/page.tsx:21-25). llm-usage is an API call inside them (src/lib/api-admin.ts:180,184), not a tab. items.title: Migrations apply at boot, but a read-only database silently skips them; whether 0243–0250 are applied in production is unknown
items.expected: Code and schema deploy together. Before the deploy, default_transaction_read_only is off, and after the boot, schema_migrations shows the newest file.
items.actual: apply_migrations runs at boot and applies pending files in filename order, one transaction per file. On a read-only server it raises ReadOnlyDatabaseError, and the app serves anyway in a DEGRADED BOOT, visible only as status 'degraded' on GET /health. Nothing in the repo monitors /health. The read-only trigger is Supabase's disk quota, and the 19 Oct sweep purge (7cab0ad4) was written because the database was near the 500 MB tier. Since 18 Oct the production branch has added 0243_reasoning_results, 0248_l1_sync_runs_coverage_index, 0249_l2_admissions and 0250_screen_followup_read_path (22 Oct). No newer migration exists on any pushed branch. Only the local-only yc2w27-s13b and yc2w27-haikufix branches carry 0250_expert_review_attempts.sql, which collides by number with production's 0250 (tests/test_migration_numbers_are_unique.py would fail on merge). The earlier 'five migrations unapplied' (0186–0190) note was superseded on 4 Oct.
evidence: git show -s 7cab0ad4 ('the DB cannot outgrow the 500 MB tier')
items.effect_on_cards: If the database went read-only, 0249 or 0250 would be missing and every card write naming their columns or tables would fail while /health only says 'degraded'. Cards would stop entirely.
items.fix: Harsh runs the read-only SQL now. Claude adds the schema head to /health (with process-live-sha-not-observable). Harsh adds an uptime monitor that alerts on /health status != ok. If STEP-13b is merged, renumber its 0250 to the next free number first.
items.blocked_on: Production read: show default_transaction_read_only; select filename, applied_at from schema_migrations where filename >= '0243' order by filename; (expected: 0243_reasoning_results, 0248_l1_sync_runs_coverage_index, 0249_l2_admissions, 0250_screen_followup_read_path).
items.correction: The mechanism is as described. migrate.py:135-180 applies files in filename order, one transaction per file, and raises ReadOnlyDatabaseError at :160-165. main.py:84-99 catches that, logs an ERROR 'DEGRADED BOOT', sets app.state.degraded_read_only and keeps serving. The only outside signal is /health returning status 'degraded'; it is logged, not silent, but no ops_alert is sent. What needs correcting is the scope of the unknown: it is wider than 0243–0250. origin/harsh/mvp sat at 84f00a40 from 11 Oct until the single push of 2026-10-21T16:19Z, and 84f00a40's newest migration is 0190_card_lane.sql. `git diff --name-status 84f00a40 origin/harsh/mvp -- migrations` lists 25 added files: 0191–0202, 0210–0212, 0220–0222, 0230, 0241–0243, 0248, 0249 and 0250. Of these, c501eec9 brought 20 (0191–0242), 0212 is the renumbered device-id migration (351de120), 0243 came with d4817942, 0248 with 1925a5bb, 0249 with fb429b78, and 0250_screen_followup_read_path with 93ea3cbe on 22 Oct. So whether all 25 are applied in production is unknown, not just 0243–0250. The 0250 collision is confirmed. Local-only yc2w27-s13b and yc2w27-haikufix carry 0250_expert_review_attempts.sql, and tests/test_migration_numbers_are_unique.py:21-27 would fail on a merge. The 7cab0ad4 subject reads '…the DB cannot outgrow the 500 MB tier', and its body says the database 'sat at 999 MB of a 500 MB tier'.
items.verify_note: The read-only SQL to settle it needs Rohit's permission: select filename from schema_migrations where filename >= '0191' order by filename; show default_transaction_read_only;

items.title: The three CI guards GeniOS-008 requires (card guard, situation-writer ratchet, model-site guard) do not exist
items.expected: CI fails when a card of a switched type does not trace to a ReasoningResult, when the list of nine situation writers in context/ grows, or when a model call appears outside the places the architecture allows.
items.actual: No test lists the nine writers as a ratchet. No test ties a card to a ReasoningResult. No commit mentions L0-5. The nearest guard is tests/test_every_llm_call_site_is_metered.py, a register that fails on any new model call site for billing reasons, but it does not check the architecture's layer placement.
evidence: git log --all --grep='L0-5' → only 3bcc1179 (the plan) and d4817942 (merge message)

grep -rl 'outreach_situations' tests | xargs grep -l situation_bso | xargs grep -l meeting_touch → tests/test_nothing_is_written_and_never_read.py, tests/context/test_situation_publisher.py (neither is a ratchet)
items.effect_on_cards: New situation-forming sites or model calls in the old places can be added without CI noticing, and that keeps the 'L2 and L3 fail each other' split alive.
items.fix: Build the three guards as AST-based tests: (1) a ratchet over the nine named writers (count can only fall); (2) a placement map, site to allowed package, checked against SITE_MARKERS and the metering register; (3) for each type switched to L2, every card's file has an admitted reasoning_results row (a Postgres test on the golden tenant). Each needs a mutation check.
items.correction: The card guard and the layer-placement guard are indeed missing. tests/test_every_llm_call_site_is_metered.py is a metering register: it does turn CI red on any new model-call module, but it is not checked against 00-ARCHITECTURE. No test asserts that a card of a switched type traces to a ReasoningResult; tests/reason/l2/* test the L2 path's behaviour, not that invariant. A situation-writer ratchet does exist in partial form under another name. tests/context/test_situation_importance.py:505-547 (`test_a_new_writer_of_context_situations_has_to_be_ranked_too`) runs in CI's test and database jobs. It fails when any module under genios_engine/ or scripts/ contains 'insert into context_situations' outside its 5 known modules (situations, periodic, support_situations, meeting_touch, document_register), and also fails when a declared one stops writing. It is not the 9-writer list in 02-MIGRATION-PLAN L3-2. It misses writers that refresh or update rows (age_uncorrelated_situations, situation_bso.refresh_situation_importance, lifecycle/store.apply_lifecycle) and writers that go through a helper (outreach via support_situations._upsert). It is also not shrink-only. tests/context/test_l2_must_not_regress.py:547 lists the same 5 modules, but only for the axis columns. Minor: `git log --all -F --grep='L0-5'` returns nothing at all, not 3bcc1179/d4817942; pickaxe -S'L0-5' shows the text was added by 3bcc1179, and no commit implements it.

items.title: There is no release gate for a 'fully functional' product
items.expected: A release passes only with all of these: (a) CI green on the exact SHA deployed; (b) a capped real-model golden pass on every model site the release changed, with the scorecard kept; (c) production health numbers the next day: pipeline_health --require-data, receipts exercised, and cards per day within a band of the baseline; (d) one card path per situation type, switched one type at a time with a one-line rollback and the old path deleted; (e) a canary tenant (Rohit's org) first, then the rest.
items.expected_source: Task brief (release-gate definition); STEP-17-TO-BUILD-real-tests.md §3.4, §4; speedrun008/GeniOS-008/01-RULES.md Rule 2.2–2.5
items.actual: (a) Not enforced (process-prod-branch-unprotected-red-ci-ships). (b) Manual, and never run on production's models (process-no-real-model-pass-on-card-sites). (c) Manual scripts with no runner (process-no-daily-production-card-health). (d) Several card paths are live together: deliver/pipeline.build_cards_for_org builds signal cards, situation-lane cards (cards_from_situations), question cards and file cards, reason/team/emit.py writes cards itself, and l2_cards adds an L2 path. (e) Per-tenant switches give a canary for features only. Prompt and code changes such as the 19 Oct junk-gate rewrite (0d5939d1) reach every tenant on deploy, because l1_llm_gate is a global bool.
evidence: genios_engine/deliver/pipeline.py:340, 419, 799, 881 (question cards, file-card versioning, build_cards_for_org, situation lane)
genios_engine/deliver/store.py:28,40 (SITUATION_CARD_BUILDER team.emit.v1, QUESTION_CARD_BUILDER); genios_engine/reason/team/emit.py (second cards writer)
items.effect_on_cards: Each deploy is a blind change to every tenant's cards, and nothing says whether a release made cards better or worse.
items.fix: Write the gate as one script, scripts/release_gate.py, that exits 0 only if: the CI run for the SHA is green (GitHub API); the scorecards in GeniOS-008/scores cover each site whose prompt hash changed since the last release; the deployed /health SHA matches; and the next day's pipeline_health --require-data plus the card-volume band pass on the canary org. Put prompt changes behind a per-tenant switch or a canary org list. Track the single-card-path cutover per situation type in GeniOS-008 03-LOG.
items.verify_note: deliver/pipeline.py has _build_question_cards at :340, _version_file_card at :419, build_cards_for_org at :799 and the cards_from_situations lane at :881. deliver/store.py:28 has SITUATION_CARD_BUILDER='team.emit.v1' and :40 QUESTION_CARD_BUILDER. reason/team/emit.py:239/292 writes `insert into cards` directly, outside CardStore.insert_card; its callers are reason/team/passes.py and reason/meetings/passes.py. l2_cards is at l4_activation.py:122. config.py:233 'l1_llm_gate: bool = True' is global. Each sub-claim (a)–(e) is backed by the sibling items verified here.

items.title: GeniOS-008 A2/A3 + GeniOS-009 D5/D6: the cutover is per tenant and covers every type at once, not one situation type at a time
items.expected: New path built beside the old one in shadow, scored by the golden set, then switched one situation type at a time, starting with 'awaiting reply / outreach'. G0.2: l2_cards on one tenant, then admission gates one type.
items.expected_source: speedrun008/GeniOS-008/03-QUESTIONS.md A2, A3; layer-2-reasoning/00-START-HERE.md L2-Q4, L2-I2; GeniOS-009/08-DECISIONS.md D5, D6; 09-HARSH-HANDOVER.md §4 G0
items.actual: `l2_cards` is a per-tenant switch with no situation-type filter. Once on, every admitted L2 judgment of every file becomes that file's review and card. L3 admissions are written in shadow only. Their reader `admitted()` has no production caller, and context_health declares it unreached ('nothing makes a card from it yet'). No per-type gate exists anywhere.
evidence: genios_engine/reason/l2/sweep.py:330-333 (makes_cards = FEATURE_L2_CARDS in activated; no type filter in the loop)
grep: the only l2_admissions readers are context/l2_admission.py:200 and the erasure list api/account_routes.py:942
items.fix: Rohit confirms A3: is the first type still awaiting-reply/outreach, or does l2_cards stay all-types for his org? Then Claude adds a per-type gate: l2_cards admits a file's card only for situation types on a per-tenant allow-list, and admission reads it. Then Harsh switches l2_reasoning → l2_cards on Rohit's org (D6).
items.blocked_on: Production state of the switches: select feature, enabled_at, disabled_at from l4_activation where org_id='<ORG>';
items.effect_on_cards: With l2_cards on, every file's card changes at once, so a regression in one type cannot be isolated. With it off (the default), no L2 judgment reaches a card. That is one reason Rohit sees 'sometimes no reasoning'.
items.mistake: The L2 rebuild (C1) built the cutover as a whole-tenant switch, against 01-RULES Rule 2 and A2's 'one situation type at a time'. The per-type gate in G0.2 has no unit.
items.correction: The detail 'every admitted judgment becomes the file's review and card' is not exact. sweep.py:378-384 writes the file review for any judgment L3 ADMITTED **or REJECTED**, unless one of its admissions is a HOLD. A rejected judgment ('nothing owed') becomes a review that stands the old lane down and makes no card. The L2 path also does more than shadow writes: record_interpretations (l2_admission.py:176-196) appends rows to situation_interpretations. It still never touches context_situations. l2_cards takes effect only when expert_review is also on, because the expert sweep returns early without it (reason/expert/sweep.py:166, 171).
items.verify_note: There is no per-type gate. reason/l2/sweep.py:332 `makes_cards = FEATURE_L2_CARDS in activated`, and the loop at :381-384 has no situation-type filter. l2_admission.admitted (context/l2_admission.py:204) has no production caller: the only other l2_admissions hit is the erasure list at api/account_routes.py:942, and context_health.py:37-40 lists it as UNREACHED. l4_activation.py:117-122 confirms the switches default off and says 'the switch to live is per situation type' with no code behind it.

Retirement is marked 'at cutover' (L2-H2), and there is no per-type cutover (see l2-a2-a3). The golden runner forces the decider on for every org, so 63/67 measures a configuration production runs only if the env var is set. Whether it is on in production was asked in YC-II 07 §9 and L2 04-FOR-HARSH §3.1 and never answered. B9/F274: its 400/day cap is per process and has no dollar governor (Rohit's call). F230: its lane rides on the model's own confidence.

speedrun008/YC-II W27/07-WHAT-IS-DONE.md §9 row 'is GENIOS_L4_LLM_DECISION_MAKER on in production?'
items.fix: Harsh reports the production env value. Rohit confirms A5 (retire). Claude then (a) makes the golden runner run the production configuration, or scores both, and (b) removes R-1 from the lanes as each type cuts over, so B9/F274 and F230 become moot.
